akhfash:25-25.t:
He said ﴿وَٱلْهَدْيَ مَعْكُوفاً﴾ (conjoined) on "and they barred" ﴿الهَدْيَ مَعْكُوفاً﴾ (the sacrificial animals, detained), out of aversion ﴿أَن يَبْلُغَ مَحِلَّهُ﴾ (to its reaching its place of sacrifice).
And He said ﴿أَن تَطَئُوهُمْ﴾ as a badal (substitute): "were it not for men — that you trample them".

akhfash:29-29.t: And He said ﴿أَخْرَجَ شَطْأَهُ فَآزَرَهُ﴾: He means (the pattern) "أَفْعَلَه" from "الإِزارَة" (supporting).

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ﴾ We decreed the conquest of Mecca and other places in the future, by force, through your jihad ﴿فَتْحًا مُبِينًا﴾ clear, manifest.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿لِيَغْفِرَ لَكَ اللَّهُ﴾ through your jihad ﴿مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِكَ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ﴾ of it, so that you may make your community desirous of jihad. It is to be interpreted figuratively, because of the infallibility of the prophets, blessings and peace be upon them, from sins, by decisive rational proof. The lām is for the final cause (al-ʿilla al-ghāʾiyya), so what it governs is an effect, not a cause ﴿وَيُتِمَّ﴾ through the conquest mentioned ﴿نِعْمَتَهُ﴾ His bestowal ﴿عَلَيْكَ وَيَهْدِيَكَ﴾ by it ﴿صِرَاطًا﴾ a path ﴿مُسْتَقِيمًا﴾ He makes you firm upon it, and it is the religion of Islam.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَيَنْصُرَكَ اللَّهُ﴾ by it ﴿نَصْرًا عَزِيزًا﴾ possessed of might, with no humiliation in it.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ السَّكِينَةَ﴾ tranquillity ﴿فِي قُلُوبِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ لِيَزْدَادُوا إِيمَانًا مَعَ إِيمَانِهِمْ﴾ in the laws of the religion: whenever one of them came down, they believed in it, and among them is jihad ﴿وَلِلَّهِ جُنُودُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ so if He had wished to help His religion through others than you, He would have done so ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيمًا﴾ of His creation ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ in His making; i.e. He has always been described thus.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿لِيُدْخِلَ﴾ attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, i.e. «أَمَرَ بِالْجِهَادِ» ("He commanded jihad") ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَيُكَفِّرَ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا﴾

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَيُعَذِّبَ الْمُنَافِقِينَ وَالْمُنَافِقَاتِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ وَالْمُشْرِكَاتِ الظَّانِّينَ بِاللَّهِ ظَنَّ السَّوْءِ﴾ with fatḥa and with ḍamma on the sīn in the three places; they thought that He would not help Muhammad ﷺ and the believers ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ دَائِرَةُ السَّوْءِ﴾ with humiliation and punishment ﴿وَغَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَعَنَهُمْ﴾ He removed them far away ﴿وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ جَهَنَّمَ وَسَاءَتْ مَصِيرًا﴾ i.e. a place of return.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ جُنُودُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا﴾ in His dominion ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ in His making; i.e. He has always been described thus.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ شَاهِدًا﴾ over your community on the Day of Resurrection ﴿وَمُبَشِّرًا﴾ to them in this world of the Garden ﴿وَنَذِيرًا﴾ a warner, making whoever does evil in it fear the Fire.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿لِيُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ [لِتُؤْمِنُوا], in it and in the three after it ﴿وَيُعَزِّرُوهُ﴾ and help him; and it was read with two zāys with the tāʾ [وَتُعَزِّزُوهُ] ﴿وَيُوَقِّرُوهُ﴾ honour him; their pronoun refers to Allah or to His Messenger [وَتُوَقِّرُوهُ] ﴿وَتُسَبِّحُوهُ﴾ i.e. Allah [وَيُسَبِّحُوهُ] ﴿بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا﴾ in the morning and the evening. [Translator's note: the source quotes the ayah with yāʾ in the first three verbs and tāʾ in «وَتُسَبِّحُوهُ», with the other reading in brackets; it is translated as printed.]

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُبَايِعُونَكَ﴾ the Pledge of Riḍwān at al-Ḥudaybiya ﴿إِنَّمَا يُبَايِعُونَ اللَّهَ﴾ it is like {مَنْ يُطِعِ الرَّسُولَ فَقَدْ أَطَاعَ اللَّهَ} ﴿يَدُ اللَّهِ فَوْقَ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ with which they pledged allegiance to the Prophet, i.e. He, Exalted is He, is aware of their pledge and will reward them for it ﴿فَمَنْ نَكَثَ﴾ broke the pledge ﴿فَإِنَّمَا يَنْكُثُ﴾ the evil consequence of his breaking it returns ﴿عَلَى نَفْسِهِ وَمَنْ أَوْفَى بِمَا عَاهَدَ عَلَيْهُ اللَّهَ فَسَيُؤْتِيهِ﴾ with yāʾ and with nūn ﴿أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿سَيَقُولُ لَكَ الْمُخَلَّفُونَ مِنَ الْأَعْرَابِ﴾ around Medina, i.e. those whom Allah held back from accompanying you when you asked them to go out with you to Mecca, fearing that Quraysh would confront you, in the year of al-Ḥudaybiya, when you return from it: ﴿شَغَلَتْنَا أَمْوَالُنَا وَأَهْلُونَا﴾ from going out with you ﴿فَاسْتَغْفِرْ لَنَا﴾ Allah, for not going out with you. He, Exalted is He, said, belying them: ﴿يَقُولُونَ بِأَلْسِنَتِهِمْ﴾ i.e. the request for forgiveness and what preceded it ﴿مَا لَيْسَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ so they are lying in their excuse ﴿قُلْ فَمَنْ﴾ an interrogative with the meaning of negation, i.e. no one ﴿يَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا إِنْ أَرَادَ بِكُمْ ضَرًّا﴾ with fatḥa and with ḍamma on the ḍād ﴿أَوْ أَرَادَ بِكُمْ نَفْعًا بَلْ كَانَ اللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ i.e. He has always been described thus.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿بَلْ﴾ in both places is for moving from one purpose to another ﴿ظَنَنْتُمْ أَنْ لَنْ يَنْقَلِبَ الرَّسُولُ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ إِلَى أَهْلِيهِمْ أَبَدًا وَزُيِّنَ ذَلِكَ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾ i.e. that they would be wiped out by killing and not return ﴿وَظَنَنْتُمْ ظَنَّ السَّوْءِ﴾ this and other things ﴿وَكُنْتُمْ قَوْمًا بُورًا﴾ the plural of «بَائِر», i.e. perishing in the sight of Allah because of this thought.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَمَنْ لَمْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ فَإِنَّا أَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ سَعِيرًا﴾ an intense fire.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا﴾ i.e. He has always been described by what has been mentioned.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿سَيَقُولُ الْمُخَلَّفُونَ﴾ who were mentioned ﴿إِذَا انْطَلَقْتُمْ إِلَى مَغَانِمَ﴾ they are the spoils of Khaybar ﴿لِتَأْخُذُوهَا ذَرُونَا﴾ let us ﴿نَتَّبِعْكُمْ﴾ so that we may take some of them ﴿يُرِيدُونَ﴾ by that ﴿أَنْ يُبَدِّلُوا كَلَامَ اللَّهِ﴾ and in one reading [كَلِمَ اللَّهِ] with kasra on the lām, i.e. His promises of the spoils of Khaybar to the people of al-Ḥudaybiya specifically ﴿قُلْ لَنْ تَتَّبِعُونَا كَذَلِكُمْ قَالَ اللَّهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ i.e. before our return ﴿فَسَيَقُولُونَ بَلْ تَحْسُدُونَنَا﴾ that we should get some of the spoils with you, so you said that ﴿بَلْ كَانُوا لَا يَفْقَهُونَ﴾ of the religion ﴿إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾ among them.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿قُلْ لِلْمُخَلَّفِينَ مِنَ الْأَعْرَابِ﴾ who were mentioned, as a test: ﴿سَتُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى قَوْمٍ أُولِي﴾ possessors of ﴿بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾ it is said they are Banū Ḥanīfa, the people of al-Yamāma, and it is said Persia and Rome ﴿تُقَاتِلُونَهُمْ﴾ an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), which in meaning is what they are called to ﴿أَوْ﴾ they ﴿يُسْلِمُونَ﴾ so you do not fight ﴿فَإِنْ تُطِيعُوا﴾ to fight them ﴿يُؤْتِكُمُ اللَّهُ أَجْرًا حَسَنًا وَإِنْ تَتَوَلَّوْا كَمَا تَوَلَّيْتُمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ يُعَذِّبْكُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ painful.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَى الْأَعْمَى حَرَجٌ وَلَا عَلَى الْأَعْرَجِ حَرَجٌ وَلَا عَلَى الْمَرِيضِ حَرَجٌ﴾ in abandoning jihad ﴿وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ يُدْخِلْهُ﴾ with yāʾ and with nūn ﴿جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّ يُعَذِّبْهُ﴾ with yāʾ and with nūn ﴿عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿لَقَدْ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذْ يُبَايِعُونَكَ﴾ at al-Ḥudaybiya ﴿تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ﴾ it was an acacia (samura), and they were one thousand three hundred or more; he then took their pledge that they would fight Quraysh and not flee from death ﴿فَعَلِمَ﴾ Allah ﴿مَا فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ of sincerity and loyalty ﴿فَأَنْزَلَ السَّكِينَةَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَثَابَهُمْ فَتْحًا قَرِيبًا﴾ it is the conquest of Khaybar after their departure from al-Ḥudaybiya.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَمَغَانِمَ كَثِيرَةً يَأْخُذُونَهَا﴾ from Khaybar ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا﴾ i.e. He has always been described thus.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَعَدَكُمُ اللَّهُ مَغَانِمَ كَثِيرَةً تَأْخُذُونَهَا﴾ from the conquests ﴿فَعَجَّلَ لَكُمْ هَذِهِ﴾ the spoils of Khaybar ﴿وَكَفَّ أَيْدِيَ النَّاسِ عَنْكُمْ﴾ regarding your families when you went out and the Jews intended [harm] against them, so Allah cast terror into their hearts ﴿وَلِتَكُونَ﴾ i.e. the hastened [spoils]; conjoined to something implied (muqaddar), i.e. «لِتَشْكُرُوهُ» ("so that you may thank Him") ﴿آيَةً لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ in their being helped ﴿وَيَهْدِيَكُمْ صِرَاطًا مُسْتَقِيمًا﴾ i.e. the path of reliance upon Him and of entrusting the matter to Him, Exalted is He.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَأُخْرَى﴾ an adjective of an implied (muqaddar) «مَغَانِمَ» (spoils); a mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿لَمْ تَقْدِرُوا عَلَيْهَا﴾ they are from Persia and Rome ﴿قَدْ أَحَاطَ اللَّهُ بِهَا﴾ He knew that they would be yours ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرًا﴾ i.e. He has always been described thus.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿وَلَوْ قَاتَلَكُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ at al-Ḥudaybiya ﴿لَوَلَّوُا الْأَدْبَارَ ثُمَّ لَا يَجِدُونَ وَلِيًّا﴾ to guard them ﴿وَلَا نَصِيرًا﴾

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun) emphasising the content of the clause before it, namely the defeat of the disbelievers and the help of the believers, i.e. «سَنَّ اللَّهُ ذَلِكَ سُنَّةً» ("Allah has established that as a way") ﴿الَّتِي قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّةِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا﴾ from Him.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي كَفَّ أَيْدِيَهُمْ عَنْكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ بِبَطْنِ مَكَّةَ﴾ at al-Ḥudaybiya ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ أَنْ أَظْفَرَكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ for eighty of them went around your camp to strike at you, and they were seized and brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he pardoned them and let them go, and that was the cause of the truce ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرًا﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ [تَعْمَلُونَ]; i.e. He has always been described thus.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿هُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوكُمْ عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ﴾ i.e. from reaching it ﴿وَالْهَدْيَ﴾ conjoined to «كُمْ» ﴿مَعْكُوفًا﴾ held back; a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿أَنْ يَبْلُغَ مَحِلَّهُ﴾ i.e. its place where it is customarily slaughtered, which is the Ḥaram; a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) ﴿وَلَوْلَا رِجَالٌ مُؤْمِنُونَ وَنِسَاءٌ مُؤْمِنَاتٌ﴾ present in Mecca with the disbelievers ﴿لَمْ تَعْلَمُوهُمْ﴾ to be characterised by faith ﴿أَنْ تَطَئُوهُمْ﴾ i.e. that you would kill them along with the disbelievers had you been permitted the conquest; a badal ishtimāl of «هُمْ» ﴿فَتُصِيبَكُمْ مِنْهُمْ مَعَرَّةٌ﴾ i.e. a sin ﴿بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾ on your part of it. The third-person pronouns are for both kinds, with the masculine given precedence (taghlīb); and the apodosis (jawāb) of «لَوْلَا» is omitted, i.e. «لَأَذِنَ لَكُمْ فِي الْفَتْحِ» ("He would have permitted you the conquest"), but it was not permitted at that time ﴿لِيُدْخِلَ اللَّهُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ such as the believers mentioned ﴿لَوْ تَزَيَّلُوا﴾ had they been separated from the disbelievers ﴿لَعَذَّبْنَا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ﴾ of the people of Mecca at that time, by permitting you its conquest ﴿عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ painful.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿إِذْ جَعَلَ﴾ attached (mutaʿalliq) to «عَذَّبْنَا» ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ the fāʿil (agent) ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْحَمِيَّةَ﴾ disdain for something ﴿حَمِيَّةَ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ﴾ a badal (substitute) of «الْحَمِيَّةَ»; it was their barring the Prophet and his Companions from the Sacred Mosque ﴿فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ وَعَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ so they made a truce with them on condition that they return the following year, and they were not overtaken by the zealotry that overtook the disbelievers, such that they would fight them ﴿وَأَلْزَمَهُمْ﴾ the believers ﴿كَلِمَةَ التَّقْوَى﴾ «لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ» ("There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah"); it is attached in a genitive construct to «التَّقْوَى» because it is its cause ﴿وَكَانُوا أَحَقَّ بِهَا﴾ more entitled to the word than the disbelievers ﴿وَأَهْلَهَا﴾ an explicative conjunction (ʿaṭf tafsīr) ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمًا﴾ i.e. He has always been described thus, and among what He, Exalted is He, knows is that they are its people.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿لَقَدْ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ الرُّؤْيَا بِالْحَقِّ﴾ the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw in sleep, in the year of al-Ḥudaybiya before setting out, that he and his Companions would enter Mecca in safety, shaving and shortening [their hair]. He told his Companions of that and they rejoiced. When they went out with him and the disbelievers barred them at al-Ḥudaybiya, and they returned, that weighed heavily on them, and some of the hypocrites doubted; so it was revealed. His saying «بِالْحَقِّ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «صَدَقَ» or is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الرُّؤْيَا», and what follows it is its explanation: ﴿لَتَدْخُلُنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرَامَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ for blessing ﴿آمِنِينَ مُحَلِّقِينَ رُءُوسَكُمْ﴾ i.e. all their hair ﴿وَمُقَصِّرِينَ﴾ some of their hair; and these are two anticipated ḥāls (ḥālān muqaddaratān) ﴿لَا تَخَافُونَ﴾ ever ﴿فَعَلِمَ﴾ in the truce ﴿مَا لَمْ تَعْلَمُوا﴾ of benefit ﴿فَجَعَلَ مِنْ دُونِ ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the entry ﴿فَتْحًا قَرِيبًا﴾ it is the conquest of Khaybar; and the vision was fulfilled the following year.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ بِالْهُدَى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ﴾ i.e. the religion of truth ﴿عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ﴾ over all the remaining religions ﴿وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا﴾ that you are sent with what has been mentioned.

celaleyn:29-29.t: As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿مُحَمَّدٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿رَسُولُ اللَّهِ﴾ its khabar (predicate) ﴿وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُ﴾ i.e. his Companions among the believers; a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is ﴿أَشِدَّاءُ﴾ harsh ﴿عَلَى الْكُفَّارِ﴾ they show them no mercy ﴿رُحَمَاءُ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ a second khabar, i.e. sympathetic to and loving one another, like a father with his child ﴿تَرَاهُمْ﴾ you see them ﴿رُكَّعًا سُجَّدًا﴾ two ḥāls (circumstantials) ﴿يَبْتَغُونَ﴾ resumptive (mustaʾnaf); they seek ﴿فَضْلًا مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْوَانًا سِيمَاهُمْ﴾ their marks; a mubtadaʾ ﴿فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ﴾ its khabar; it is a light and whiteness by which they will be known in the Hereafter as having prostrated in this world ﴿مِنْ أَثَرِ السُّجُودِ﴾ attached (mutaʿalliq) to that to which the khabar is attached, i.e. «كَائِنَةً» ("being"), and it is parsed as a ḥāl from its pronoun that has moved over to the khabar ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the description mentioned ﴿مَثَلُهُمْ﴾ their description ﴿فِي التَّوْرَاةِ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar ﴿وَمَثَلُهُمْ فِي الْإِنْجِيلِ﴾ a mubtadaʾ; its khabar is: ﴿كَزَرْعٍ أَخْرَجَ شَطْأَهُ﴾ with sukūn and with fatḥa on the ṭāʾ; its offshoots ﴿فَآزَرَهُ﴾ with the long vowel and the short; strengthened and supported it ﴿فَاسْتَغْلَظَ﴾ became thick ﴿فَاسْتَوَى﴾ became strong and upright ﴿عَلَى سُوقِهِ﴾ its stalks; the plural of «سَاق» ﴿يُعْجِبُ الزُّرَّاعَ﴾ i.e. its sowers, because of its beauty. The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, were likened to this because they began few and weak, then grew many and strong in the best of ways ﴿لِيَغِيظَ بِهِمُ الْكُفَّارَ﴾ attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted indicated by what precedes it, i.e. «شُبِّهُوا بِذَلِكَ» ("they were likened to that") ﴿وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ مِنْهُمْ﴾ i.e. the Companions; «مِنْ» is for explaining the genus (bayān al-jins), not partitive, because all of them have the description mentioned ﴿مَغْفِرَةً وَأَجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾ the Garden; and these two are also for those after them, in [other] ayahs.

daas-irab:1-5.t: ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿فَتَحْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿لَكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿فَتْحاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿مُبِيناً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿لِيَغْفِرَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit an after the lām. ﴿لَكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām of causation (taʿlīl), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to فتحنا. ﴿تَقَدَّمَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنْ ذَنْبِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَما تَأَخَّرَ﴾ conjoined to mā taqaddama. ﴿وَيُتِمَّ﴾ conjoined to yaghfira. ﴿نِعْمَتَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَيَهْدِيَكَ﴾ conjoined to yaghfira; the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi and its fāʿil is latent. ﴿صِراطاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مُسْتَقِيماً﴾ an adjective. ﴿وَيَنْصُرَكَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it, and the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. ﴿نَصْراً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq. ﴿عَزِيزاً﴾ an adjective. ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنْزَلَ السَّكِينَةَ﴾ a past verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فِي قُلُوبِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لِيَزْدادُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an implicit an after the lām of causation, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿إِيماناً﴾ tamyīz (specification); the interpreted maṣdar from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām of causation, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to anzala. ﴿مَعَ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān). ﴿إِيمانِهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلِلَّهِ﴾ a resumptive particle, and a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar. ﴿جُنُودُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to السماوات; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَكانَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its noun. ﴿عَلِيماً حَكِيماً﴾ two khabars of kāna; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿لِيُدْخِلَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an implicit an after the lām of causation, with its fāʿil latent; the interpreted maṣdar from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām of causation, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to something omitted, its implied form being "He commanded jihad in order to admit" (amara بالجهاد li-yudkhila). ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ﴾ conjoined to المؤمنين. ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is an adjective of جنات. ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl. ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خالدين. ﴿وَيُكَفِّرَ﴾ a conjunction, and conjoined to yudkhila. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿سَيِّئاتِهِمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَكانَ﴾ the wāw of circumstance, and a defective past verb. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ its noun. ﴿عِنْدَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَوْزاً﴾ the khabar of kāna. ﴿عَظِيماً﴾ an adjective; the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:6-9.t: ﴿وَيُعَذِّبَ﴾ a conjunction, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿الْمُنافِقِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَالْمُنافِقاتِ﴾ conjoined to المنافقين. ﴿وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ وَالْمُشْرِكاتِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿الظَّانِّينَ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) الظانين. ﴿ظَنَّ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿السَّوْءِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿دائِرَةُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿السَّوْءِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَغَضِبَ اللَّهُ﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَلَعَنَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it, and the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَساءَتْ﴾ a resumptive particle, and a past verb of blame (dhamm) whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿مَصِيراً﴾ tamyīz (specification); the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلِلَّهِ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a fronted khabar. ﴿جُنُودُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to السماوات; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزاً حَكِيماً﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and kāna, its noun and its two khabars; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿أَرْسَلْناكَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿شاهِداً﴾ ḥāl. ﴿وَمُبَشِّراً وَنَذِيراً﴾ conjoined to شاهدا. ﴿لِتُؤْمِنُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit an after the lām of causation (taʿlīl); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أرسلناك. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to تؤمنوا. ﴿وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَتُعَزِّرُوهُ وَتُوَقِّرُوهُ وَتُسَبِّحُوهُ﴾ conjoined to تؤمنوا. ﴿بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا﴾ two adverbs of time (ẓarfā zamān).

daas-irab:10-11.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿يُبايِعُونَكَ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِنَّما﴾ a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿يُبايِعُونَ اللَّهَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the Name of Majesty is its object; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿يَدُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). [Translator's note: the source prints the word with a fatḥa (اللَّهَ); as muḍāf ilayhi it is اللَّهِ.] ﴿فَوْقَ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān). ﴿أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the nominal clause is a second khabar of inna. ﴿فَمَنْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and a conditional noun causing the jussive, a mubtadaʾ. ﴿نَكَثَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿فَإِنَّما﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis of the condition, and إنما is a restraining particle and the restrained one. ﴿يَنْكُثُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the two clauses of the protasis and the apodosis are the khabar of man. ﴿عَلى نَفْسِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ a conjunction, and a conditional noun causing the jussive, a mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَوْفى﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿عاهَدَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَلَيْهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the ṣila. ﴿فَسَيُؤْتِيهِ﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis, the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb and its first object. ﴿أَجْراً﴾ its second object. ﴿عَظِيماً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, and the two clauses of the protasis and the apodosis are the khabar of man. ﴿سَيَقُولُ﴾ the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). ﴿لَكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْمُخَلَّفُونَ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنَ الْأَعْرابِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to المخلفون. ﴿شَغَلَتْنا أَمْوالُنا﴾ a past verb and its object, and أموالنا is its fāʿil. ﴿وَأَهْلُونا﴾ conjoined to أموالنا; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فَاسْتَغْفِرْ﴾ a conjunction, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿بِأَلْسِنَتِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لَيْسَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent. ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of laysa; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿فَمَنْ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَمْلِكُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, the nominal clause is the object of the saying, and the clause qul is resumptive. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to yamliku. ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to yamliku. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿أَرادَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿ضَرًّا﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿أَرادَ بِكُمْ نَفْعاً﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿كانَ اللَّهُ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خبيرا. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿خَبِيراً﴾ the khabar of kāna; the clause kāna is resumptive.

daas-irab:12-14.t: ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī). ﴿ظَنَنْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿أَنْ﴾ lightened from the heavy anna; its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), omitted. ﴿لَنْ يَنْقَلِبَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by lan. ﴿الرَّسُولُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ conjoined to الرسول; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of an. ﴿إِلى أَهْلِيهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿أَبَداً﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of ظننتم, and the clause ظننتم is resumptive. ﴿وَزُيِّنَ ذلِكَ﴾ a conjunction, and a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَظَنَنْتُمْ﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿ظَنَّ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿السَّوْءِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَكُنْتُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and kāna and its noun. ﴿قَوْماً﴾ its khabar. ﴿بُوراً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ a resumptive particle, and a conditional noun causing the jussive, a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لَمْ يُؤْمِنْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, with its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَإِنَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of causation (taʿlīl), and inna and its noun. ﴿أَعْتَدْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿لِلْكافِرِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿سَعِيراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar of inna, the nominal clause is a causal explanation, and the two clauses of the protasis and the apodosis are the khabar of man. ﴿وَلِلَّهِ﴾ a resumptive particle, and a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar. ﴿مُلْكُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to السماوات. ﴿يَغْفِرُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿لِمَنْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent, the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the clause yaghfiru is resumptive. ﴿وَيُعَذِّبُ﴾ conjoined to yaghfiru, with its fāʿil latent. ﴿مَنْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and kāna, its noun and its two khabars; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿سَيَقُولُ الْمُخَلَّفُونَ﴾ the sīn is a particle of the future, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِذَا﴾ an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿انْطَلَقْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿إِلى مَغانِمَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿لِتَأْخُذُوها﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit an after the lām of causation (taʿlīl); the wāw is its fāʿil and hā its object; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to انطلقتم. ﴿ذَرُونا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and nā its object. ﴿نَتَّبِعْكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab); the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause ذرونا is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿يُرِيدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنْ يُبَدِّلُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿كَلامَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the interpreted maṣdar from an and the verb is the object of يريدون. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَنْ تَتَّبِعُونا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by lan; the wāw is its fāʿil and nā its object; the clause is the object of the saying, and the clause qul is resumptive. ﴿كَذلِكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿قالَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿فَسَيَقُولُونَ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, the sīn is a particle of the future, and an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb) or conjunction. ﴿تَحْسُدُونَنا﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and nā its object; the clause is conjoined to سيقولون. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَفْقَهُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of كانوا, and the clause كانوا is resumptive. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿لِلْمُخَلَّفِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مِنَ الْأَعْرابِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to المخلفين; the clause is resumptive. ﴿سَتُدْعَوْنَ﴾ the sīn is for the future, and a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿إِلى قَوْمٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to تدعون. ﴿أُولِي﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of qawm, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ because it is treated like the sound masculine plural. ﴿بَأْسٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿شَدِيدٍ﴾ an adjective of بأس. ﴿تُقاتِلُونَهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its object; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يُسْلِمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَإِنْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and in is a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿تُطِيعُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿يُؤْتِكُمُ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive in that it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ its fāʿil. ﴿أَجْراً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿حَسَناً﴾ an adjective; the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and in is a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿تَتَوَلَّوْا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the protasis, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿كَما﴾ the kāf is a particle of comparison and of the genitive, and mā is maṣdariyya (yielding a verbal noun). ﴿تَوَلَّيْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from mā and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the kāf, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to tawallaytum. ﴿يُعَذِّبْكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis; the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi and its fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَذاباً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq. ﴿أَلِيماً﴾ an adjective; the clause is the apodosis of a jussive-causing condition, not joined to the fāʾ, and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:17-18.t: ﴿لَيْسَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿عَلَى الْأَعْمى﴾ the fronted khabar (predicate) of laysa. ﴿حَرَجٌ﴾ its postponed noun; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلا عَلَى الْأَعْرَجِ حَرَجٌ وَلا عَلَى الْمَرِيضِ حَرَجٌ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and man is a conditional noun causing the jussive, a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُطِعِ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), with its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir). ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ conjoined to the Name of Majesty. ﴿يُدْخِلْهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the two clauses of the protasis and the apodosis are the khabar of man, and the clause yudkhilhu is the apodosis with no grammatical position, because it is not joined to the fāʾ. ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of جنات, and the nominal clause man… is resumptive. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿مَنْ يَتَوَلَّ يُعَذِّبْهُ عَذاباً أَلِيماً﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لَقَدْ﴾ the lām falls in the answer to the oath, and qad is a particle of realization (taḥqīq). ﴿رَضِيَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil. ﴿عَنِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the answer to the oath. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿يُبايِعُونَكَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and the kāf its object; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿تَحْتَ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān). ﴿الشَّجَرَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَعَلِمَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted [element that is the] ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿فَأَنْزَلَ السَّكِينَةَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَأَثابَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its first object, with its fāʿil latent. ﴿فَتْحاً﴾ its second object. ﴿قَرِيباً﴾ an adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:19-21.t: ﴿وَمَغانِمَ﴾ a conjunction, and conjoined to فتحا. ﴿كَثِيرَةً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿يَأْخُذُونَها﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent) and hā its object; the clause is an adjective of مغانم. ﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزاً حَكِيماً﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and kāna, its noun and its two khabars (predicates); the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَعَدَكُمُ﴾ a past verb and its object. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, a postponed fāʿil. ﴿مَغانِمَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿كَثِيرَةً﴾ an adjective; the clause is resumptive. ﴿تَأْخُذُونَها﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its object; the clause is an adjective of مغانم. ﴿فَعَجَّلَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿هذِهِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَكَفَّ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿أَيْدِيَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿النَّاسِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عَنْكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلِتَكُونَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by the implicit an after the lām of causation (taʿlīl), its noun being latent. ﴿آيَةً﴾ its khabar. ﴿لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to kaffa. ﴿وَيَهْدِيَكُمْ﴾ a conjunction, and an imperfect verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent. ﴿صِراطاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مُسْتَقِيماً﴾ an adjective; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَأُخْرى﴾ a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لَمْ تَقْدِرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿عَلَيْها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is an adjective of أخرى. ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of realization (taḥqīq). ﴿أَحاطَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and kāna, with the Name of Majesty as its noun. ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to قديرا. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قَدِيراً﴾ the khabar of kāna; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:22-24.t: ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and law is a conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿قاتَلَكُمُ﴾ a past verb and its object. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ its fāʿil (agent); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لَوَلَّوُا﴾ the lām falls in the apodosis of the condition, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿الْأَدْبارَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَجِدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿وَلِيًّا﴾ its object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and lā is redundant (zāʾida). ﴿نَصِيراً﴾ conjoined to waliyyan. ﴿سُنَّةَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الَّتِي﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of sunna. ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of realization (taḥqīq). ﴿خَلَتْ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَلَنْ تَجِدَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by lan, with its fāʿil latent. ﴿لِسُنَّةِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to تبديلا. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿تَبْدِيلًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive. ﴿كَفَّ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿أَيْدِيَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَنْكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بِبَطْنِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مَكَّةَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to kaffa. ﴿أَنْ﴾ a maṣdar-forming particle causing the accusative. ﴿أَظْفَرَكُمْ﴾ a past verb in the position of the accusative; the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi and its fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and kāna, with the Name of Majesty as its noun. ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to بصيرا. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿بَصِيراً﴾ the khabar of kāna; the clause is the ṣila, and the clause kāna is resumptive.

daas-irab:25-25.t: ﴿هُمُ الَّذِينَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَصَدُّوكُمْ﴾ conjoined to كفروا. ﴿عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْحَرامِ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of al-masjid. ﴿وَالْهَدْيَ﴾ mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), and the wāw is for accompaniment (maʿiyya). ﴿مَعْكُوفاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَنْ يَبْلُغَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an, with its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿مَحِلَّهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). ﴿وَلَوْلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and لولا is a conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿رِجالٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted. ﴿مُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ an adjective. ﴿وَنِساءٌ مُؤْمِناتٌ﴾ conjoined to رجال مؤمنون. ﴿لَمْ تَعْلَمُوهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ a mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَنْ تَطَؤُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an; the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its object; the interpreted maṣdar from an and the verb is a badal (substitute) of the hāʾ in تعلموهم. ﴿فَتُصِيبَكُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb conjoined to what precedes it, and the kāf is its object. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مَعَرَّةٌ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿بِغَيْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl of the object of تصيبكم. ﴿عِلْمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لِيُدْخِلَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an implicit an after the lām of causation (taʿlīl). ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its fāʿil. ﴿فِي رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مَنْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the interpreted maṣdar from an and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to something omitted and implied. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿لَوْ﴾ a conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿تَزَيَّلُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿لَعَذَّبْنَا﴾ the lām falls in the apodosis of the condition, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis of law and has no grammatical position. [Translator's note: the source reads «جواب لولا محل لها», evidently «جواب لو لا محل لها» run together.] ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿عَذاباً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿أَلِيماً﴾ an adjective.

daas-irab:26-27.t: ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿جَعَلَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) جعل. ﴿الْحَمِيَّةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿حَمِيَّةَ﴾ badal (substitute). ﴿الْجاهِلِيَّةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَأَنْزَلَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its fāʿil. ﴿سَكِينَتَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿عَلى رَسُولِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَعَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَأَلْزَمَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its first object, with its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿كَلِمَةَ﴾ its second object. ﴿التَّقْوى﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَكانُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and kāna and its noun. ﴿أَحَقَّ﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿بِها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أحق. ﴿وَأَهْلَها﴾ conjoined to أحق. ﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and kāna and its noun. ﴿بِكُلِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to عليما. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَلِيماً﴾ the khabar of kāna; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿لَقَدْ﴾ the lām falls in the answer to an omitted oath, and qad is a particle of realization (taḥqīq). ﴿صَدَقَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its fāʿil. ﴿رَسُولَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الرُّؤْيا﴾ accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to صدق; the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿لَتَدْخُلُنَّ﴾ the lām of the answer to the omitted oath, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the nūn that is dropped because of the succession of like letters; the dropped wāw is its fāʿil, and the nūn is for emphasis; the clause is the answer to an omitted oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿الْمَسْجِدَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْحَرامَ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿شاءَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its fāʿil; the verbal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because the context indicates it. ﴿آمِنِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مُحَلِّقِينَ﴾ a second ḥāl. ﴿رُؤُسَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَمُقَصِّرِينَ﴾ conjoined to محلقين. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿تَخافُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is circumstantial. ﴿فَعَلِمَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿ما﴾ its object; the clause is conjoined to صدق. ﴿لَمْ تَعْلَمُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فَجَعَلَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَتْحاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿قَرِيباً﴾ an adjective.

daas-irab:28-29.t: ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الَّذِي﴾ its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَرْسَلَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿رَسُولَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بِالْهُدى﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَدِينِ﴾ conjoined to الهدى. ﴿الْحَقِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لِيُظْهِرَهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit an after the lām of causation (taʿlīl), and the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَلَى الدِّينِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿كُلِّهِ﴾ a tawkīd (emphasis) of الدين; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to arsala. ﴿وَكَفى﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a past verb. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ genitive in form, nominative in position, the fāʿil of كفى. ﴿شَهِيداً﴾ tamyīz (specification); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿مَعَهُ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān). ﴿أَشِدَّاءُ﴾ khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿عَلَى الْكُفَّارِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أشداء. ﴿رُحَماءُ﴾ a second khabar. ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place, attached to رحماء. ﴿تَراهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿رُكَّعاً سُجَّداً﴾ two ḥāls. ﴿يَبْتَغُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَضْلًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to فضلا. ﴿وَرِضْواناً﴾ conjoined to فضلا. ﴿سِيماهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿مِنْ أَثَرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿السُّجُودِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿ذلِكَ مَثَلُهُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿فِي التَّوْراةِ﴾ ḥāl; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَمَثَلُهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِي الْإِنْجِيلِ﴾ ḥāl. ﴿كَزَرْعٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَخْرَجَ شَطْأَهُ﴾ a past verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of زرع. ﴿فَآزَرَهُ﴾ a past verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is conjoined to akhraja. ﴿فَاسْتَغْلَظَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَاسْتَوى﴾ also conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿عَلى سُوقِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to استوى. ﴿يُعْجِبُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿الزُّرَّاعَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لِيَغِيظَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by the implicit an after the lām of causation, with its fāʿil latent. ﴿بِهِمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْكُفَّارِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. [Translator's note: the source prints the word with a kasra (الْكُفَّارِ); as mafʿūl bihi it is الْكُفَّارَ.] The interpreted maṣdar from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to وعد. ﴿وَعَدَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila, and the clause وعد is resumptive. ﴿وَعَمِلُوا﴾ conjoined to آمنوا. ﴿الصَّالِحاتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿مَغْفِرَةً﴾ the second mafʿūl bihi of وعد. ﴿وَأَجْراً﴾ conjoined to maghfira. ﴿عَظِيماً﴾ an adjective.

dervis-irab:17-21.t:
* I'rab:
(لَيْسَ عَلَى الْأَعْمى حَرَجٌ وَلا عَلَى الْأَعْرَجِ حَرَجٌ وَلا عَلَى الْمَرِيضِ حَرَجٌ) A resumptive discourse, offered to explain the ruling concerning the disabled and those with infirmities with respect to jihad, and to remove blame from them for staying behind from it. لَيْسَ is a defective past verb; عَلَى الْأَعْرَجِ is the fronted khabar (predicate) of لَيْسَ, and حَرَجٌ is its postponed ism (subject); what follows is conjoined to it. The order was observed with regard to which of these is most deserving of having blame lifted from him: so الْأَعْمى was put first because his excuse is obvious and lasting and any benefit from him is entirely absent; and الْأَعْرَجِ was put before الْمَرِيضِ because the infirmity of lameness may in certain situations still allow some benefit, such as guard duty and the like, whereas as for the sick person, the possibility of the illness leaving him is expected at any time.
(وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ يُدْخِلْهُ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ) The waw is a conjunction; مَنْ is conditional, in the position of a nominative mubtadaʾ (subject); يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and يُدْخِلْهُ is its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); جَنَّاتٍ is a second direct object (mafʿūl bihi), in the broad sense; and the clause تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ is an adjective (naʿt) of جَنَّاتٍ.
(وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّ يُعَذِّبْهُ عَذاباً أَلِيماً) Conjoined to what preceded.
(لَقَدْ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذْ يُبايِعُونَكَ تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ) A resumptive discourse, to affirm the pleasure [of Allah] with those who pledged allegiance; for that reason it was named the Pledge of Riḍwān (Good Pleasure), and its details are in the books of biography and history. The lām is the one that prepares for an oath; قَدْ is a particle of certainty; رَضِيَ اللَّهُ is a verb and agent; عَنِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ are both attached to رَضِيَ; إِذْ is an adverb of past time attached to رَضِيَ; and the clause يُبايِعُونَكَ is the genitive-construct complement (muḍāf ilayhi) of the adverb. The context would have required the past tense, but it departed from it for a secret that will come in the section on rhetoric. تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ is an adverbial attached to يُبايِعُونَكَ.
(فَعَلِمَ ما فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ فَأَنْزَلَ السَّكِينَةَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَثابَهُمْ فَتْحاً قَرِيباً) The fāʾ is a conjunction; عَلِمَ is a past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", referring to Allah the Exalted, and the clause is conjoined to يُبايِعُونَكَ, because, as preceded, it has the sense of the past. مَا is a relative noun, a direct object; فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ are both attached to an omitted predicate which is the ṣila (relative clause) of مَا. فَأَنْزَلَ is conjoined to فَعَلِمَ; السَّكِينَةَ is a direct object; وَأَثابَهُمْ is likewise a conjoined verb, the hā is a first direct object, فَتْحاً is a second direct object, and قَرِيباً is an adjective.
(وَمَغانِمَ كَثِيرَةً يَأْخُذُونَها وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزاً حَكِيماً) The waw is a conjunction; مَغانِمَ is conjoined to فَتْحاً قَرِيباً; the clause يَأْخُذُونَها is an adjective of مَغانِمَ; and وَكانَ with its ism and khabar.
(وَعَدَكُمُ اللَّهُ مَغانِمَ كَثِيرَةً تَأْخُذُونَها) A resumptive discourse in the manner of iltifāt (shift of address). وَعَدَكُمُ اللَّهُ is a past verb, a fronted direct object and a postponed agent; مَغانِمَ is a second direct object; كَثِيرَةً is an adjective; and the clause تَأْخُذُونَها is a second adjective.
(فَعَجَّلَ لَكُمْ هذِهِ وَكَفَّ أَيْدِيَ النَّاسِ عَنْكُمْ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; عَجَّلَ is a past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun referring to Allah; لَكُمْ are both attached to عَجَّلَ; هذِهِ is a direct object; and وَكَفَّ أَيْدِيَ النَّاسِ عَنْكُمْ is conjoined to what preceded.
(وَلِتَكُونَ آيَةً لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَيَهْدِيَكُمْ صِراطاً مُسْتَقِيماً) The waw is conjoined to something implied, i.e. "so that you may thank Him"; according to the Kufans it is interpolated (muqḥama). The ism of تَكُونَ is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "it", and آيَةً is its khabar; لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ is an adjective of آيَةً; وَيَهْدِيَكُمْ is conjoined to وَلِتَكُونَ, the kāf is a first direct object, and صِراطاً مُسْتَقِيماً is a second direct object.
(وَأُخْرى لَمْ تَقْدِرُوا عَلَيْها قَدْ أَحاطَ اللَّهُ بِها وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيراً) وَأُخْرى: the waw is a conjunction, and أُخْرى is conjoined to هذِهِ, i.e. "He hastened for you these spoils, and other spoils". They also permitted أُخْرى to be a mubtadaʾ, with the clause لَمْ تَقْدِرُوا عَلَيْها as its adjective and the clause قَدْ أَحاطَ اللَّهُ بِها as its khabar. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is permissible for أُخْرى to be accusative by a concealed verb that is explained by قَدْ أَحاطَ اللَّهُ بِها, its implied form being: 'and Allah decreed another which He has encompassed.'" They also permitted it to be genitive through an implied rubba, the waw being the waw of rubba; and concerning the noun made genitive after the waw of rubba there is a well-known disagreement, whether it is by an implied rubba or by the waw itself. Abū Ḥayyān said, in the course of refuting this i'rab: "This is strange, because rubba has never come in the Qur'an as a genitive-governing particle, despite its frequent occurrence in the speech of the Arabs; so how could it be brought in as implied?" Al-Qurtubi confined himself to the first view. The wording of Abu al-Baqaʾ is: "وَأُخْرى means 'and He promised you another', or 'He rewarded you with another'; it may also be a mubtadaʾ, with لَمْ تَقْدِرُوا as the adjective and قَدْ أَحاطَ as the khabar." وَكانَ with its ism and khabar; and عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ are both attached to قَدِيراً.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «إذ يبايعونك» there is a departure from the imperfect to the past, and the secret in it is to bring the scene of the pledge vividly to mind, because it deserves to be embodied so that it may be a lesson from the grandfathers to the grandchildren. The gist of its story is that when the Prophet ﷺ camped at al-Ḥudaybiya, having seen the failure of the Quraysh envoys in their efforts and the loss of their counsel to their people, he sent Khirāsh ibn Umayya al-Khuzāʿī as a messenger to Mecca. Then the most wretched of the Quraysh at that time, ʿIkrima ibn Abī Jahl, rose up, hamstrung the envoy's she-camel and intended to kill him, had not some of them intervened, rescued him and sent him back to his people. When the Prophet ﷺ saw him, he called ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, in order to send him. ʿUmar said: "I fear them for myself," because of what was known of his enmity toward them, "but I will direct you to a man who is mightier there than I and dearer to them: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān." So he sent him, provided him with a letter from himself explaining the purpose of his coming, and charged him to visit the oppressed Muslims of Mecca, consoling them and urging patience until the victory and the conquest of Allah should come. The embassy of ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, did not turn the Quraysh from their resolve; they persisted in their obstinacy, determined to prevent the Messenger and his Companions from circumambulating, whatever the outcome, and the most they allowed was to permit ʿUthmān alone to circumambulate the House. ʿUthmān refused unless he would be in the company of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. This statement enraged the Quraysh and stirred their anger, so they ordered ʿUthmān imprisoned for three days until they could consider his case. The people passed the news along, exaggerated, until it reached the Messenger's camp that ʿUthmān had been killed. At this the Prophet ﷺ stood up to speak, saying: "If what we heard is true, we shall not leave until we fight the people. The pledge, the pledge, O people!" The people streamed in to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ beneath the tree, which was a samura (acacia) tree. The first to pledge to him was Sinān al-Asadī, who said to him as he pledged: "I pledge to you on what is in my soul." The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "And what is in your soul?" Sinān said: "To strike with my sword before you until Allah makes you victorious, or I am killed." The people pledged on what Sinān had pledged, and the number of those who pledged was one thousand five hundred and twenty-five... and so on to the end of that delightful story, to which whoever wishes may return in the books of biography.

* Benefits:
Ibn Saʿd related, with a sound chain of transmission, on the authority of Nāfiʿ, that it reached ʿUmar that some people were coming to the tree and praying beside it; so he threatened them, then ordered it cut down, and it was cut down. The wisdom in that is that no temptation (fitna) may arise through it.

dervis-irab:22-26.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْهَدْيَ) Its explanation has preceded. It has three forms, which Ibn Khalawayh reported: الهَدْي, which is the well-known one; الهَدِيّ with a doubled yāʾ; and الهَداء. It is what is brought as a gift to the Kaʿba.
(مَعْكُوفاً) Detained. One says "ʿakaftu the man from his need" when you have held him back from it. Al-Fārisī denied that ʿakafa can take its object directly, but he is refuted, as al-Azharī and Ibn Sīda say, by the formation of the passive participle from it.
(مَعَرَّةٌ) The form mafʿala, from ʿarrahu, meaning ʿarāhu, when something he dislikes befalls him. In al-Qāmūs and Lisān [al-ʿArab]: al-maʿarra is harm, sin, injury, crime, defect, an ugly matter, hardship, abuse, the face changing colour out of anger, a star below the Milky Way, and a well-known town.

* I'rab:
(وَلَوْ قاتَلَكُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوَلَّوُا الْأَدْبارَ ثُمَّ لا يَجِدُونَ وَلِيًّا وَلا نَصِيراً) The waw is resumptive; لَوْ is conditional; قاتَلَكُمُ is a verb with a fronted direct object, and الَّذِينَ is the agent, and the clause كَفَرُوا is the ṣila. In لَوَلَّوُا the lām occurs in the apodosis of لَوْ; وَلَّوُا is a verb and agent, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of لَوْ; الْأَدْبارَ is a direct object. ثُمَّ is a conjunction; لا is a negative particle; يَجِدُونَ is an imperfect nominative verb with its agent; وَلِيًّا is a direct object; and وَلا نَصِيراً is conjoined to it.
(سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّةِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا) سُنَّةَ is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) because it is an emphatic maṣdar, i.e. "Allah established the victory of His prophets as an established way". الَّتِي is an adjective of سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ, and the clause قَدْ خَلَتْ is the ṣila of الَّتِي; مِنْ قَبْلُ are both attached to خَلَتْ. The waw is a conjunction; لَنْ is a particle of negation, accusative-governing and of future sense; تَجِدَ is an imperfect verb made accusative by لَنْ; لِسُنَّةِ اللَّهِ are both attached to تَجِدَ; and تَبْدِيلًا is a direct object.
(وَهُوَ الَّذِي كَفَّ أَيْدِيَهُمْ عَنْكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ بِبَطْنِ مَكَّةَ مِنْ بَعْدِ أَنْ أَظْفَرَكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ) A resumptive discourse. وَهُوَ is a mubtadaʾ and الَّذِي its khabar; the clause كَفَّ is the ṣila; أَيْدِيَهُمْ is a direct object; عَنْكُمْ are both attached to كَفَّ; and وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ is conjoined to أَيْدِيَهُمْ عَنْكُمْ. بِبَطْنِ مَكَّةَ specifies the place, which is al-Ḥudaybiya, so it is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "being in the heart of Mecca"; al-Ḥudaybiya adjoins the Sanctuary. مِنْ بَعْدِ are both attached to كَفَّ as well; أَنْ and what is within its scope are in the position of a genitive by annexation to the adverb; and عَلَيْهِمْ are both attached to أَظْفَرَكُمْ.
(وَكانَ اللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيراً) كانَ with its ism, and بَصِيراً is its khabar; بِما تَعْمَلُونَ are both attached to بَصِيراً.
(هُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوكُمْ عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ وَالْهَدْيَ مَعْكُوفاً أَنْ يَبْلُغَ مَحِلَّهُ) A resumptive discourse to identify those who barred the Prophet ﷺ from the Sacred Mosque. هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ and الَّذِينَ its khabar; the clause كَفَرُوا is the ṣila; وَصَدُّوكُمْ is conjoined to the ṣila; عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ are both attached to صَدُّوكُمْ, and الْحَرامِ is an adjective. وَالْهَدْيَ is conjoined to the accusative pronoun in صَدُّوكُمْ, which is the kāf; it may also be a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), the waw being the waw of accompaniment; and مَعْكُوفاً is a ḥāl. As for أَنْ يَبْلُغَ, أَنْ and what is within its scope are in the sense of a maṣdar made accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "from reaching" or "(held back) from reaching"; and in that case it is permissible for this implied preposition to be attached to صَدُّوكُمْ or to be attached to مَعْكُوفاً, i.e. "detained from reaching its place". It is also permissible for the interpreted maṣdar to be in the position of an accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), because it is the reason for the barring, the implied form being "they barred the sacrificial animals out of dislike that it should reach its place", or it is the reason for مَعْكُوفاً, i.e. "in order that it reach its place". Some parsed it as a badal al-ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from الْهَدْيَ, i.e. "(they obstructed) the reaching of the sacrificial animals to their place".
(وَلَوْلا رِجالٌ مُؤْمِنُونَ وَنِساءٌ مُؤْمِناتٌ لَمْ تَعْلَمُوهُمْ أَنْ تَطَؤُهُمْ) The waw is a conjunction; وَلَوْلا is a particle of prevention due to existence; رِجالٌ is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "present in Mecca"; مُؤْمِنُونَ is an adjective of رِجالٌ; and نِساءٌ مُؤْمِناتٌ is conjoined to رِجالٌ مُؤْمِنُونَ; the clause لَمْ تَعْلَمُوهُمْ is an attribute of the men and women together; and أَنْ and what is within its scope are in the sense of a maṣdar, a badal al-ishtimāl from them or from the accusative pronoun in تَعْلَمُوهُمْ.
(فَتُصِيبَكُمْ مِنْهُمْ مَعَرَّةٌ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ of cause; تُصِيبَكُمْ is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أَنْ after the fāʾ of cause, and the kāf is a direct object; مِنْهُمْ are both attached to تُصِيبَكُمْ; مَعَرَّةٌ is the agent of تُصِيبَكُمْ; and بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ are both attached to an omitted ḥāl from the kāf, or to an omitted adjective of مَعَرَّةٌ. The discussion of the apodosis of لَوْلا will come.
(لِيُدْخِلَ اللَّهُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ لَوْ تَزَيَّلُوا لَعَذَّبْنَا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ عَذاباً أَلِيماً) The lām is for cause; يُدْخِلَ is an imperfect made accusative by an optionally implied أَنْ after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to something implied, i.e. "the absence of empowerment over the people of Mecca and the absence of punishment were so that Allah might admit...", so it is the reason for what was indicated by the restraining of hands, understood from the context, from the people of Mecca, to protect the believers who were in it. فِي رَحْمَتِهِ are both attached to يُدْخِلَ; مَنْ يَشاءُ is a direct object, and the clause يَشاءُ is the ṣila. لَوْ is conditional; تَزَيَّلُوا is a past verb and agent, i.e. "if some of them had been distinguished from others"; the lām is the linking lām; the clause عَذَّبْنَا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of لَوْ, and it indicates the apodosis of لَوْلا (more on this discussion will come in the section on rhetoric). عَذَّبْنَا is a verb and agent; الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا is a direct object; مِنْهُمْ is a ḥāl; عَذاباً is a mafʿūl muṭlaq; and أَلِيماً is an adjective.
(إِذْ جَعَلَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْحَمِيَّةَ حَمِيَّةَ الْجاهِلِيَّةِ) إِذْ is an adverb of past time attached to عَذَّبْنَا, or to صَدُّوهُمْ عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ; you may also make it accusative with an implied "remember"; and the clause جَعَلَ is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. الَّذِينَ is the agent, and the clause كَفَرُوا is the ṣila. فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ are both attached to جَعَلَ if it has the meaning "cast", or to an omitted second direct object of جَعَلَ if it has the meaning "made"; الْحَمِيَّةَ is a first direct object; and حَمِيَّةَ الْجاهِلِيَّةِ is a badal (substitute). الْحَمِيَّةُ is disdain; one says "ḥamītu from such-and-such" ḥamiyya when you disdain it and shame and disdain at doing it enter you. Al-Mutalammis said:
ألا إنني منهم وعرضي عرضهم ... كذا الرأس يحمي أنفه أن يهشما
(Indeed I am of them, and my honour is their honour; so the head protects its nose from being crushed.)
(فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلى رَسُولِهِ وَعَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَأَلْزَمَهُمْ كَلِمَةَ التَّقْوى وَكانُوا أَحَقَّ بِها وَأَهْلَها) The fāʾ is conjoined to something implied that is indispensable, understood from the context, i.e. "the Muslims were about to oppose the word of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ regarding the treaty, and entered thereby into a ruinous matter, or doubt crept into their hearts, so He sent down...". اللَّهُ is its agent; سَكِينَتَهُ is a direct object; عَلى رَسُولِهِ are both attached to أَنْزَلَ; عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ is conjoined to what preceded; وَأَلْزَمَهُمْ is likewise conjoined, the hā is a first direct object, and كَلِمَةَ التَّقْوى is a second direct object (what is meant by it will come in the section on benefits); وَكانُوا is conjoined to what preceded; أَحَقَّ is the khabar of كانُوا; بِها are both attached to أَحَقَّ; and أَهْلَها is conjoined to أَحَقَّ as an explicative conjunction.
(وَكانَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيماً) كانَ with its ism; بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ are both attached to عَلِيماً; and عَلِيماً is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there are subtle points of meaning, namely that He the Exalted made clear the greatest distance between the disbeliever and the believer. He set them apart in the two agents, for the agent of "made" is the disbelievers, and the agent of "sent down" is Allah the Exalted; and in the two objects, for that is disdain and this is tranquillity; and in the two annexations, for He annexed disdain to the Jāhiliyya (Age of Ignorance) and annexed tranquillity to Allah the Exalted; and in the two verbs, "made" and "sent down": for disdain is made in the moment, an accident that does not last, whereas tranquillity is like something preserved in the treasury of mercy, which He sent down. Disdain is ugly and blameworthy in itself and grew uglier by being annexed to the Jāhiliyya, and tranquillity is good in itself and grew better by being annexed to Allah the Exalted. The conjunction in «فأنزل» with fāʾ and not waw indicates correspondence: you say "Zayd honoured me so I honoured him", which indicates recompense by way of correspondence, and for that reason «فأنزل» was used. Since the Messenger ﷺ was the one who first responded to the treaty, while the believers were resolved on fighting and not returning to their families except after the conquest of Mecca or slaughtering at the place of slaughter, and refused anything but writing "Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ" and "In the name of Allah", the Exalted said «على رسوله». And when he ﷺ became calm about the treaty, the believers became calm, so He said «وعلى المؤمنين». And since the believers in the sight of Allah the Exalted were bound to that word, the Exalted said «إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم».

dervis-irab:27-29.t:
* Vocabulary:
(شَطْأَهُ) With sukūn on the ṭāʾ and with fatḥa on it; both are among the seven canonical readings. In al-Mukhtār: "the shatʾ of crops and plants is their shoots; al-Akhfash said: their tip; and ashtaʾa al-zarʿ means its shatʾ came out." In al-Qāmūs: al-shatʾ is the shoots of the palm and of crops, or its leaf; shataʾa, like manaʿa, shatʾan and shuṭūʾan, means it put them forth; and of a tree, what comes out around its base, the plural being ashṭāʾ; ashtaʾa means it put them forth; and of a man, his child reached maturity and became like him.

* I'rab:
(لَقَدْ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ الرُّؤْيا بِالْحَقِّ) The lām is the one that prepares for an oath; قَدْ is a particle of certainty; صَدَقَ اللَّهُ is a verb and agent; رَسُولَهُ is a direct object; and الرُّؤْيا is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "in his vision". It was also said that kadhaba takes two objects: one says "kadhabanī al-ḥadīth", and likewise ṣadaqa, as in the verse, but this is unusual because it is not known for the lightened form to take two objects and the doubled form one. The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: "ṣadaqa takes two objects, the second directly or by a preposition: you say ṣadaqtu Zaydan al-ḥadīth and ṣadaqtuhu fī al-ḥadīth." This is what al-Qāmūs follows. The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: "He confirmed him in his vision and did not belie him, Allah being exalted far above falsehood and every ugliness; so the preposition was dropped and the verb made to reach [the object], as in His saying the Exalted: صَدَقُوا ما عاهَدُوا اللَّهَ عَلَيْهِ." بِالْحَقِّ is attached to صَدَقَ or is a ḥāl from الرُّؤْيا.
(لَتَدْخُلُنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرامَ إِنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ آمِنِينَ مُحَلِّقِينَ رُؤُسَكُمْ وَمُقَصِّرِينَ لا تَخافُونَ) The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; تَدْخُلُنَّ is an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the presence of the nūn, which was omitted because of the succession of similar letters since it is one of the five verbs; the waw, omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the agent; the nūn is the nūn of heavy emphasis; الْمَسْجِدَ is a direct object in the broad sense, and الْحَرامَ is an adjective. إِنْ is conditional, شاءَ اللَّهُ is the protasis, and the apodosis is omitted because what precedes indicates it. Concerning the suspension of the promise on [Allah's] will, although He the Exalted is the creator of all things and knows them before they occur, there are views that we summarize as follows: 1. It is a report of the words of the angel to the Messenger ﷺ; said by Ibn Kaysān. 2. This suspension is good manners taught by Allah the Exalted, even though what was promised is certain to occur, as He the Exalted said: «ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا إلا أن يشاء الله». 3. Thaʿlab said: He made an exception in what He knows so that creatures might make exceptions in what they do not know. 4. The Kufans claimed that إِنْ here has the meaning of إِذْ, which is mentioned to give the reason for what precedes it; they said it is not conditional because a condition is in the future and this story has already passed. The most correct of what is said is what al-Zamakhsharī reported, whose text is: "If you say: what is the point of the entry of 'if Allah wills' into a report from Allah, mighty and majestic? I say: there are several aspects to it: that He suspends His promise on the will, to teach His servants to say the same in their promises, adopting the good manners of Allah and following His practice." آمِنِينَ is a ḥāl from the waw omitted from لَتَدْخُلُنَّ because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, i.e. a ḥāl concurrent with the entering, and the condition is parenthetical; the meaning is "secure at the time of entering". مُحَلِّقِينَ is a second, nested ḥāl; رُؤُسَكُمْ is a direct object; لا is a negative particle; and تَخافُونَ is an imperfect verb, nominative by the presence of the nūn, and the clause is resumptive or a ḥāl from the agent of لَتَدْخُلُنَّ, or from the pronoun in آمِنِينَ or in مُحَلِّقِينَ.
(فَعَلِمَ ما لَمْ تَعْلَمُوا فَجَعَلَ مِنْ دُونِ ذلِكَ فَتْحاً قَرِيباً) The fāʾ is conjoined to the clause صَدَقَ اللَّهُ; عَلِمَ is a past verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "he"; مَا is a direct object, and the clause لَمْ تَعْلَمُوهُ is the ṣila of مَا. فَجَعَلَ: the fāʾ is a conjunction; مِنْ دُونِ ذلِكَ are both attached to جَعَلَ; فَتْحاً is a direct object; and قَرِيباً is an adjective.
(هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ بِالْهُدى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ) هُوَ is a mubtadaʾ and الَّذِي its khabar; the clause أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ is the ṣila of the relative; بِالْهُدى are both attached to an omitted ḥāl from the direct object, i.e. "bearing the guidance"; وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ is conjoined to الْهُدى. The lām is for cause; يُظْهِرَهُ is an imperfect made accusative by an implied أَنْ after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أَرْسَلَ, i.e. "to make it prevail over the religion in its entirety". كُلِّهِ is an emphasis (tawkīd) of الدِّينِ, and the al in الدِّينِ is generic, meaning the various religions.
(وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيداً) كَفى is a past verb; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; the name of Majesty is genitive in form and an agent of كَفى in position; and شَهِيداً is a tamyīz.
(مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُ أَشِدَّاءُ عَلَى الْكُفَّارِ رُحَماءُ بَيْنَهُمْ) مُحَمَّدٌ is a mubtadaʾ and رَسُولُ اللَّهِ its khabar; وَالَّذِينَ is a mubtadaʾ; مَعَهُ is an adverbial attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila; أَشِدَّاءُ is a khabar; عَلَى الْكُفَّارِ are both attached to أَشِدَّاءُ; رُحَماءُ is a second khabar; and بَيْنَهُمْ is an adverbial attached to رُحَماءُ, plural of raḥīm.
(تَراهُمْ رُكَّعاً سُجَّداً يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًا مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْواناً) The clause is a third khabar, and you may make it resumptive. تَراهُمْ is an imperfect verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "you", and the hā is a direct object; رُكَّعاً سُجَّداً are two ḥāls. The clause يَبْتَغُونَ is resumptive, as if it were the answer to a question arising from their persistence in bowing and prostrating, as if it were said "what do they want by that?" and so was said "they seek...", or it is a third ḥāl. فَضْلًا is a direct object; مِنَ اللَّهِ are both attached to يَبْتَغُونَ; and رِضْواناً is conjoined to فَضْلًا.
(سِيماهُمْ فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ مِنْ أَثَرِ السُّجُودِ) سِيماهُمْ is a mubtadaʾ; it has three forms, al-sīmā, al-sīmāʾ and al-sīmiyāʾ, and it means the mark. فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ is the khabar; and مِنْ أَثَرِ السُّجُودِ is a ḥāl.
(ذلِكَ مَثَلُهُمْ فِي التَّوْراةِ) ذلِكَ is a mubtadaʾ, the indication being to the description just given, namely their being stern and merciful, and their mark being on their faces; مَثَلُهُمْ is its khabar; and فِي التَّوْراةِ is a ḥāl.
(وَمَثَلُهُمْ فِي الْإِنْجِيلِ كَزَرْعٍ أَخْرَجَ شَطْأَهُ فَآزَرَهُ فَاسْتَغْلَظَ فَاسْتَوى عَلى سُوقِهِ) وَمَثَلُهُمْ is a mubtadaʾ; فِي الْإِنْجِيلِ is a ḥāl; كَزَرْعٍ is the khabar of مَثَلُهُمْ; and the clause أَخْرَجَ شَطْأَهُ is an adjective of زَرْعٍ. There are other i'rab views, whose mention will come in the section on benefits. فَآزَرَهُ is conjoined to أَخْرَجَ, and likewise فَاسْتَغْلَظَ and His saying فَاسْتَوى; عَلى سُوقِهِ are both attached to اسْتَوى or to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "standing upon its stalks"; and al-sūq is the plural of sāq.
(يُعْجِبُ الزُّرَّاعَ لِيَغِيظَ بِهِمُ الْكُفَّارَ) The clause is a ḥāl, i.e. while it is pleasing; الزُّرَّاعَ is the object of يُعْجِبُ. لِيَغِيظَ: the lām is for cause, and the imperfect verb is made accusative by an implied أَنْ after the lām of cause; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to a verb indicated by the context, i.e. "they were likened to that", so the cause relates to the simile. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: His saying لِيَغِيظَ بِهِمُ الْكُفَّارَ, what is it giving the reason for? I say: for what their likening to the crop indicates, of their growth and advancement in increase and strength; and it is permissible to make it the reason for Allah's promise to those who believed", so it is attached to وَعَدَ.
(وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ مِنْهُمْ مَغْفِرَةً وَأَجْراً عَظِيماً) وَعَدَ is a past verb and اللَّهُ its agent; الَّذِينَ is its object, the clause آمَنُوا is the ṣila, and the clause وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ is conjoined to the ṣila; مِنْهُمْ is a ḥāl; مَغْفِرَةً is a second direct object, or accusative by removal of the preposition (one says waʿadahu al-amr and bihi); وَأَجْراً is conjoined to مَغْفِرَةً; and عَظِيماً is an adjective.

dervis-irab:1-9.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّا فَتَحْنا لَكَ فَتْحاً مُبِيناً) «إن» and its ism; the clause «فتحنا» is its khabar (predicate). «لك» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «فتحنا»; «فتحا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and «مبينا» is a ṣifa (adjective). What is meant by the conquest is the conquest of Mecca; it was also said that it is the treaty of al-Ḥudaybiya, and a treaty may be called a conquest. The past tense was used although the conquest had not yet occurred, because Allah's, Exalted is He, report of its realisation and certainty stands in the position of what exists and has come to be; more explanation of this report will come in the section on rhetoric.
(لِيَغْفِرَ لَكَ اللَّهُ ما تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِكَ وَما تَأَخَّرَ) The lām is for purpose. «يغفر» is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «فتحنا».
