The secret of making the conquest of Mecca a cause of forgiveness will come in the section on rhetoric. «لك» is attached to «يغفر»; «الله» is the fāʿil (agent); «ما» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the clause «تقدم» is a ṣila (relative clause); «من ذنبك» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); «وما تأخر» is conjoined to «ما تقدم».
(وَيُتِمَّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكَ وَيَهْدِيَكَ صِراطاً مُسْتَقِيماً) «ويتم» is conjoined to «ليغفر»; «نعمته» is a mafʿūl bihi; «عليك» is attached to «نعمته» or to «يتم». «ويهديك» is likewise conjoined; the «كاف» is the first mafʿūl bihi and «صراطا مستقيما» is the second mafʿūl bihi, or is accusative by removal of the preposition.
(وَيَنْصُرَكَ اللَّهُ نَصْراً عَزِيزاً) Conjoined to what precedes. «نصرا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq and «عزيزا» is a naʿt (adjective). The secret of this attribution will come in the section on rhetoric.
(هُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ السَّكِينَةَ فِي قُلُوبِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ لِيَزْدادُوا إِيماناً مَعَ إِيمانِهِمْ) «هو» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «الذي» is the khabar; the clause «أنزل السكينة» is a ṣila. «في قلوب المؤمنين» is attached to «أنزل». «ليزدادوا»: the lām is for purpose and «يزدادوا» is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām. «إيمانا» is a tamyīz (specification), and «مع» is an adverb of place attached to an omitted naʿt of «إيمانا».
(وَلِلَّهِ جُنُودُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً) The «واو» is a conjunction; «لله» is a fronted khabar and «جنود السموات والأرض» a postponed mubtadaʾ. «كان الله»: «كان» and its ism; «عليما» is its first khabar and «حكيما» its second khabar.
(لِيُدْخِلَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها) The lām is for purpose; «يدخل» is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām of purpose; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element which al-Jalāl implied as "He commanded jihad in order that He may admit". The wording of Abu Hayyān: "What appears is that it is attached to an omitted element indicated by the discourse. That is because He said «ولله جنود السموات والأرض», and in that is evidence that He, Exalted is He, tests by those hosts whom He wills, so that good is accepted from the one for whom good was decreed, and evil from the one for whom evil was decreed, 'in order to admit the believers into gardens and punish the disbelievers'. So the lām is attached to this «يبتلي» and to whatever is connected with the testing, namely the acceptance of belief and of disbelief." «المؤمنين» is a mafʿūl bihi of «ليدخل»; «المؤمنات» is conjoined to «المؤمنين»; «جنات» is the second mafʿūl bihi of «ليدخل», by extension; the clause «تجري من تحتها الأنهار» is a ṣifa of «جنات»; «خالدين فيها» is a ḥāl.
(وَيُكَفِّرَ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ وَكانَ ذلِكَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ فَوْزاً عَظِيماً) Conjoined to what precedes; «سيئاتهم» is the object of «يكفر». «كان» and its ism; «فوزا عظيما» is the khabar. «عند الله» is an adverb of place attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally a ṣifa of «فوزا» and was fronted before it.
(وَيُعَذِّبَ الْمُنافِقِينَ وَالْمُنافِقاتِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ وَالْمُشْرِكاتِ الظَّانِّينَ بِاللَّهِ ظَنَّ السَّوْءِ عَلَيْهِمْ دائِرَةُ السَّوْءِ) Likewise conjoined. «الظانين» is a naʿt of «المنافقين» and «المشركين»; «بالله» is attached to «الظانين»; «ظن السوء» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq. «السَّوء» with fatḥa on the sīn means blame, and with ḍamma («السُّوء») means punishment, defeat and evil. It was also said that they are two dialects, except that the fatḥa form predominates in being annexed to what is intended to be blamed, while the ḍamma form follows the course of «الشر» (evil); and both are originally maṣdars. The annexation is not of the type of annexing the described to its description, which is not permitted according to the Basrans because the description and the described are expressions of one thing, so that annexing one of them to the other would be annexing a thing to itself; rather «السوء» is a ṣifa of an omitted described noun, i.e. "thinking the evil thing", the muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the construct) being omitted and the ṣifa put in its place. «عليهم» is a fronted khabar and «دائرة السوء» a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is optative (duʿāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. «الدائرة» is originally an expression for the danger encircling the centre, then it came to be used for the event encircling the one it befalls, although its use is predominantly for what is disliked. The annexation of «الدائرة» to «السوء» is the annexation of the general to the specific, so it is explicative, like "a ring of silver" (khātam fiḍḍa); what is meant is encirclement and encompassing, such that evil does not skip them or pass them by.
(وَغَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَعَنَهُمْ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ جَهَنَّمَ وَساءَتْ مَصِيراً) The «واو» is a conjunction; «غضب الله» is a verb and fāʿil; «عليهم» is attached to «غضب»; «ولعنهم» is likewise conjoined; «وأعد لهم جهنم» likewise conjoined; «وساءت مصيرا» likewise conjoined, and «مصيرا» is a tamyīz.
(وَلِلَّهِ جُنُودُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزاً حَكِيماً) The «واو» is resumptive; «لله» is a fronted khabar and «جنود السموات والأرض» a postponed mubtadaʾ. The i'rab of «وكان الله عزيزا حكيما» was given a little earlier. The secret of the repetition will come in the section on rhetoric.
(إِنَّا أَرْسَلْناكَ شاهِداً وَمُبَشِّراً وَنَذِيراً) «إن» and its ism; the clause «أرسلناك» is its khabar; «شاهدا» is a ḥāl; «مبشرا ونذيرا» are conjoined to «شاهدا».
(لِتُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَتُعَزِّرُوهُ وَتُوَقِّرُوهُ وَتُسَبِّحُوهُ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا) The lām is for purpose; «تؤمنوا» is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «أرسلناك», because it is the reason for the sending. «بالله» is attached to «تؤمنوا»; «ورسوله» is conjoined to «الله»; «وتعزروه» and what follows is conjoined to «لتؤمنوا». «التعزير» is support and «التوقير» is respect and veneration. All of them were read with «ياء» (the third person), the pronoun referring to the people. «بكرة وأصيلا» are two adverbs for «تسبحوه», i.e. in the morning and the evening; from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both: the dawn prayer, and the noon and afternoon prayers.

* Rhetoric:
In these verses there are lofty varieties of the sciences of rhetoric. The first:
1- Expression by the past tense: in His saying «إنا فتحنا», the report of the conquest came in the form of the past tense because it was revealed when he, peace be upon him, returned from al-Ḥudaybiya, before the year of the conquest. The secret in that is that Allah's, Exalted is He, reports, being realised, are placed in the position of what exists and has come to be, and in that is a grandeur and an indication of the lofty standing and the truthfulness of the One reporting that is not hidden from anyone with a trace of intellect.
2- Causation: Allah, Exalted is He, made the conquest of Mecca the cause of forgiveness because the conquest, in being jihad and worship, is a cause of forgiveness. It was also said that the secret in it is the gathering of the four things enumerated, namely forgiveness, the completion of the favour, guidance and the mighty help, as though it were said: "We made easy for you the conquest of Mecca and helped you against your enemy, so that the glory of both abodes and the aims of the present and the future might be gathered for you."
3- Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī): this is in His saying, Exalted is He, «وينصرك الله نصرا عزيزا». Glory and invincibility were attributed to the help, though they belong to the one helped; for the form faʿīl here is for relation, so «العزيز» means "possessing glory".
4- Repetition: Allah, Exalted is He, said first «وكان الله عليما حكيما» and said second «وكان الله عزيزا حكيما». He mentioned before the first verse «ولله جنود السموات والأرض», and since among them are some who are fit for mercy and some who are fit for punishment, it was fitting that the conclusion of the first be «وكان الله عليما حكيما». When He, Exalted is He, went to extremes in the punishment of the hypocrite and the disbeliever and its severity, it was fitting that the conclusion of the second be «وكان الله عزيزا حكيما». The first indicates that He is the Disposer of the affair of creatures in accordance with His wisdom, and the second indicates threat and menace and that they are in the grip of the Avenger. Some have tried to deny that this is a repetition, but there is no call for that, because repetition has secrets, some of which have passed, and of which there will come some that are more astonishing and more deserving of reflection.

dervis-irab:10-12.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يُبايِعُونَكَ) They pledge allegiance to you, i.e. they covenant with you. The covenant was called «مبايعة» (a sale-transaction), which is the exchange of property for property, by analogy with the transaction in that each of them includes the meaning of exchange; for the covenant also includes exchange between their undertaking to stand firm in fighting the disbelievers and his, peace be upon him, guarantee of Allah's pleasure with them and His rewarding them with the gardens of bliss in return for fighting the disbelievers. More detail will come in the section on rhetoric.
(بُوراً) «البور» is destruction. It may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a predicate of a plural, and it may be the plural of «بائر», like «حائل» and «حول», «بازل» and «بزل»; the first is more likely. It is used to describe the masculine singular, the feminine singular, the dual and the plural of both. Ibn al-Zibaʿrā said:
يا رسول المليك إن لساني ... راتق ما فتقت إذ أنا بور
(O messenger of the King, my tongue mends what I tore apart when I was in ruin.)
And «البور» of land is what has not been sown.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُبايِعُونَكَ إِنَّما يُبايِعُونَ اللَّهَ) A resumptive discourse introduced to explain that whoever pledges allegiance to the Messenger, peace be upon him, in form has pledged allegiance to Allah in reality. «إن» and its ism; the clause «يبايعونك» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. «إنما» is a restraining particle together with the thing it restrains (kāffa and makfūfa). The clause «إنما يبايعون الله» is the khabar (predicate) [Translator's note: the source writes «خبران» (dual), and misspells «يبعايعون»]. What is meant by this pledge is the Pledge of Riḍwān at al-Ḥudaybiya.
(يَدُ اللَّهِ فَوْقَ أَيْدِيهِمْ فَمَنْ نَكَثَ فَإِنَّما يَنْكُثُ عَلى نَفْسِهِ) «يد الله» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «فوق أيديهم» is an adverb attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted khabar of «يد الله». The clause is a second khabar of «إن»; it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of the agent in «يبايعونك», and it may also be resumptive. «فمن»: the «فاء» is resumptive and «من» is a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. «نكث» is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the «فاء» is a linking particle. «إنما» is a kāffa and makfūfa. «ينكث» is a nominative imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent, its implied form being "he". «على نفسه» is attached to «ينكث». The clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
(وَمَنْ أَوْفى بِما عاهَدَ عَلَيْهُ اللَّهَ فَسَيُؤْتِيهِ أَجْراً عَظِيماً) The «واو» is a conjunction; «من» is a jussive conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ; «أوفى» is the protasis, and it is in the sense of «وفى»: one says «وفى بالعهد» and «أوفى به», and it is the dialect of Tihāma. «بما» is attached to «أوفى»; the clause «عاهد» is a ṣila; «عليه» is attached to «عاهد». The «هاء» was given ḍamma although it takes kasra after a «ياء», because a sukūn follows it, so both ḍamma and kasra are permissible. The majestic name is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The «فاء» links the apodosis. «يؤتيه» is a verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; «أجرا» is the second mafʿūl bihi and «عظيما» a naʿt (adjective).
(سَيَقُولُ لَكَ الْمُخَلَّفُونَ مِنَ الْأَعْرابِ شَغَلَتْنا أَمْوالُنا وَأَهْلُونا فَاسْتَغْفِرْ لَنا) The «سين» is a particle of the future; «يقول» is a nominative imperfect verb; «لك» is attached to «يقول»; «المخلفون» is the fāʿil; «من الأعراب» is a ḥāl. The clause «شغلتنا أموالنا» is the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). «وأهلونا» is conjoined to «أموالنا», its sign of nominative being the «واو», because it is attached to the sound masculine plural, i.e. "from going out with you". «فاستغفر»: the «فاء» is a conjunction; «استغفر» is an imperative verb; «لنا» is attached to «استغفر»; the object of «استغفر» is omitted, i.e. "Allah".
(يَقُولُونَ بِأَلْسِنَتِهِمْ ما لَيْسَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ) The clause is the content of His saying. «يقولون» is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, the «واو» being the fāʿil. «بألسنتهم» is attached to «يقولون». «ما» is a mafʿūl bihi; «ليس» is a defective past verb whose ism is latent, its implied form being "it"; «في قلوبهم» is the khabar; the clause is the ṣila of «ما».
(قُلْ فَمَنْ يَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئاً إِنْ أَرادَ بِكُمْ ضَرًّا أَوْ أَرادَ بِكُمْ نَفْعاً) «قل» is an imperative verb; the «فاء» is a conjunction; «من» is an interrogative noun whose meaning is negation, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; «يملك» is an imperfect verb with a latent fāʿil, its implied form being "he", and the clause is the khabar of «من»; the clause is the content of «قل». «لكم» is attached to «يملك»; «من الله» is a ḥāl; «شيئا» is the object of «يملك». «إن» is a conditional particle and «أراد» is the protasis; the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "who then possesses". «بكم» is attached to «أراد», and «خيرا» is the object of «أراد» [Translator's note: the source writes «خيرا» here, whereas the verse has «ضرا»]. The clause «أو أراد بكم نفعا» is conjoined to the preceding clause.
(بَلْ كانَ اللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيراً) «بل» is a particle of disavowal marking transition from one topic to another. «كان» and its ism; «بما» is attached to «خبيرا»; the clause «تعملون» is a ṣila; «خبيرا» is the khabar of «كان».
(بَلْ ظَنَنْتُمْ أَنْ لَنْ يَنْقَلِبَ الرَّسُولُ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ إِلى أَهْلِيهِمْ أَبَداً) «بل» is likewise a particle of disavowal of transition: He moved away from explaining the invalidity of their excuse to explaining what led them to stay behind. «ظننتم» is a verb and fāʿil. «أن» and what is within its scope stand in the place of the two objects of «ظننتم». «أن» is the lightened form of the heavy «أنّ», with the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) as its ism. «لن» is a particle of negation, accusative and future; «ينقلب» is an imperfect verb made accusative by «لن»; «الرسول» is the fāʿil; «والمؤمنون» is conjoined to «الرسول»; «إلى أهليهم» is attached to «ينقلب»; «أبدا» is an adverb also attached to «ينقلب».
(وَزُيِّنَ ذلِكَ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ وَظَنَنْتُمْ ظَنَّ السَّوْءِ وَكُنْتُمْ قَوْماً بُوراً) «زين» is a passive past verb and «ذلك» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); «في قلوبكم» is attached to «زين». «ظننتم» is conjoined to «زين». «ظن السوء» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). «كان» and its ism; «قوما» is its khabar and «بورا» is a naʿt of «قوما».

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «إن الذين يبايعونك إنما يبايعون الله» there is an explicit derivative metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya tabaʿiyya) in the verb, as was mentioned earlier: the name "pledge of allegiance" (mubāyaʿa) was applied to this covenant. You will find its details in the books of history.
2- In His saying «يد الله فوق أيديهم» there is an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya): He, Exalted is He, likened Himself to the one pledging allegiance and affirmed for Himself what is among the concomitants of the one pledging allegiance in reality, namely the hand, by way of the original implicit metaphor. In affirming a hand for Allah, Exalted is He, while Allah is exalted above limbs and the attributes of bodies, there is a confirmation of the meaning of correspondence (mushākala).
3- In His saying «فمن يملك لكم من الله شيئا إن أراد بكم ضرّا أو أراد بكم نفعا» is the art of lafff (gathering). The original would be: "who possesses anything for you against Allah if He wills harm for you, and who would deprive you of benefit if He wills benefit for you", because the like of this structure is used for harm, and it has occurred in the Noble Book consistently so. He said: «فمن يملك من الله شيئا إن أراد أن يهلك المسيح ابن مريم», and His saying «ومن يرد الله فتنته فلن تملك له من الله شيئا». From it also is his saying, peace be upon him, in some hadith, «إنني لا أملك شيئا», addressing his clan. The secret of its being specific to the warding off of harm is that possession is annexed in these places by the lām, and warding off harm is a benefit that is attributed to the one from whom it is warded off, whereas the denial of benefit is not so, for it is a harm returning upon him, not for him. When that is clear, the verse was arranged in this manner only because the two divisions share that each of them is a negation of warding off what has been decreed, of good and of evil; so since they are close, He included them in one expression and specified the expression of warding off harm because it is what is to be expected for these people, as the verse is in the context of threat or severe menace. It is the counterpart of His saying: «قل من ذا الذي يعصمكم من الله إن أراد بكم سوءا أو أراد بكم رحمة», for protection is only from evil, not from mercy.

* Benefits:
«الأهلون»: the plural of «أهل»; one also says «أهلات», on the assumption of a feminine tāʾ, like «أرض» and «أرضات». What made this plural of «أهل» good is that it comes in the sense of a description, as in their saying «الحمد لله أهل الحمد» ("Praise be to Allah, the One worthy of praise"), and that in fact it refers to rational beings.

dervis-irab:13-16.t:
* I'rab:
(وَمَنْ لَمْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ فَإِنَّا أَعْتَدْنا لِلْكافِرِينَ سَعِيراً) The «واو» is a conjunction, to establish their ruin and explain how it comes about. «من» is a jussive conditional noun, or a relative noun, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). «لم» is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; «يؤمن» is an imperfect verb made jussive by «لم»; «بالله» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يؤمن»; «ورسوله» is conjoined to «الله». The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. "for he is a disbeliever", and the «فاء» is conjoined to the apodosis. «إن» and its ism; the clause «أعتدنا» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; «للكافرين» is attached to «أعتدنا»; «سعيرا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause of the protasis and the apodosis is the khabar of «من» if it is conditional; and the clause «فإنا أعتدنا» is the khabar if it is relative, the «فاء» entering because of the sense of condition in the relative noun.
(وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً) The «واو» is a conjunction; «لله» is a fronted khabar and «ملك السموات والأرض» a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause «يغفر» is circumstantial (ḥāl). «لمن» is attached to «يغفر»; the clause «يشاء» is a ṣila (relative clause); «ويعذب من يشاء» is conjoined to the clause of the ṣila. «كان» and its ism and its two khabars.
(سَيَقُولُ الْمُخَلَّفُونَ إِذَا انْطَلَقْتُمْ إِلى مَغانِمَ لِتَأْخُذُوها ذَرُونا نَتَّبِعْكُمْ) The «سين» is a particle of the future; «يقول المخلفون» is a verb and fāʿil (agent). «إذا» is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, attached to «يقول», i.e. "they will say at the time of your setting out". The clause «انطلقتم» is in the position of a genitive through the adverb's annexation to it. «إلى مغانم» is attached to «انطلقتم». The clause «ذرونا» is the content of their saying, i.e. «دعونا» ("let us be"); it was already mentioned that the Arabs have let die its past tense, its maṣdar and its active participle. «نتبعكم» is a jussive imperfect verb, because it is the response to a request.
(يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يُبَدِّلُوا كَلامَ اللَّهِ) The clause «يريدون» is circumstantial from the fāʿil, namely «المخلفون»; you may also make it resumptive. Abu al-Baqāʾ made it a ḥāl from the pronoun of the object in «ذرونا», and in that there is strain and remoteness. «أن» and what follows it is the object of «يريدون»; «كلام الله» is the object of «يبدلوا». In one reading, «كَلِم الله», the plural of «كلمة».
(قُلْ لَنْ تَتَّبِعُونا كَذلِكُمْ قالَ اللَّهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ) «قل» is an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "you". «لن» is a particle of negation, accusative and future; «تتبعونا» is an imperfect verb made accusative by «لن», its sign of accusative being the omission of the nūn, and the «واو» is the fāʿil and «نا» the mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the content of the saying. «كذلكم» is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a saying like this saying issued from me", namely «لن تتبعونا».
(فَسَيَقُولُونَ بَلْ تَحْسُدُونَنا بَلْ كانُوا لا يَفْقَهُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا) The «فاء» is a conjunction and the «سين» a particle of the future; «يقولون» is a nominative imperfect verb. «بل» is a particle of disavowal or conjunction; the disavowal is of its being Allah's ruling that they not follow them, and the affirmation of something worse than that, namely envy. «تحسدوننا» is conjoined to «سيقولون»; it is an imperfect verb, nominative, with fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi. The second «بل» is a disavowal of describing them by attributing envy to the believers in favour of something more serious than it, namely ignorance and lack of understanding; more of this will come in the section on rhetoric. «كان» and its ism; the clause «لا يفقهون» is its khabar; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «قليلا» is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "except a little understanding". So there is no sense in al-Jalāl's saying «إلا قليلا منهم» ("except a few of them"), because all of them share in the description of dullness and stupidity.
(قُلْ لِلْمُخَلَّفِينَ مِنَ الْأَعْرابِ سَتُدْعَوْنَ إِلى قَوْمٍ أُولِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ تُقاتِلُونَهُمْ أَوْ يُسْلِمُونَ) «قل» is an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "you". «للمخلفين» is attached to «قل»; «من الأعراب» is a ḥāl; the clause «ستدعون» is the content of the saying. The secret of the repetition will come. «إلى قوم» is attached to «تدعون»; «أولي بأس شديد» is a naʿt of «قوم»; the clause «تقاتلونهم» is a second naʿt or a ḥāl, and you may make it resumptive. «أو» is a conjunction; «يسلمون» is conjoined to «تقاتلونهم»; you may also put the imperfect verb in the nominative as resumptive, the implied form being «أو هم يسلمون», i.e. "or they submit".
(فَإِنْ تُطِيعُوا يُؤْتِكُمُ اللَّهُ أَجْراً حَسَناً) The «فاء» is a conjunction; «إن» is conditional; «تطيعوا» is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its sign of jussive being the omission of the nūn, and the «واو» is the fāʿil. «يؤتكم» is the apodosis; the «كاف» is the first mafʿūl bihi, «الله» is the fāʿil, «أجرا» is the second mafʿūl bihi, and «حسنا» is a naʿt of «أجرا».
(وَإِنْ تَتَوَلَّوْا كَما تَوَلَّيْتُمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ يُعَذِّبْكُمْ عَذاباً أَلِيماً) The «واو» is a conjunction; «إن» is conditional; «تتولوا» is the protasis. «كما» is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, and «ما» is maṣdarī; this i'rab has often been given earlier, though Sībawayh inclined to analysing the «كاف» in the like of this construction as a ḥāl. «من قبل» is attached to «توليتم», and «قبل» is indeclinable on ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning. «يعذبكم» is the apodosis, the «كاف» is its object, «عذابا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and «أليما» is a naʿt of «عذابا».

* Rhetoric:
1- Hyperbole: in His saying, Exalted is He, «فسيقولون بل تحسدوننا بل كانوا لا يفقهون إلا قليلا». The first disavowal is familiar: it is their habit and the proof of their obstinacy and their persistence in stubbornness and insistence on foolishness. As for the second disavowal, in it their dullness and stupidity take shape, because the first disavowal contains attribution to ignorance in a specific matter, namely their attributing envy to the believers, while the second contains attribution to general ignorance without restriction.
2- Repetition: He repeated the mention of the tribes who stayed behind under this name as hyperbole in blame and to show the ugliness of staying behind, as though blame keeps coming upon them whenever their mention by it is repeated and it brands them with its mark. The exegetes differed concerning these people whom they were summoned to fight and who are described as having severe might: it was said they are Hawāzin and those who fought the Messenger at Ḥunayn; it was said they are the Romans, against whom he went out in the year of Tabūk; and it was said they are the people of the apostasy, whom Abū Bakr fought. The details are to be consulted in their proper places.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ فَتْحاً مُّبِيناً﴾.
It was a victory (fatḥ) in which there was [little] fighting: a throwing of stones at one another. A fatḥ may be a peace settlement, and it may be the taking of a thing by force; and the fighting [179/a] that was meant was only on the day of al-Ḥudaybiya.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿دَآئِرَةُ ٱلسَّوْءِ﴾.
Like your saying: "a man of evil (رجل السَّوء)"; and دائرة السوء is the punishment. Al-sawʾ [with fatḥa] is more widespread and more frequent in the language, and the Arabs seldom say: دائرة السُّوء.

farraa:8-9.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ شَاهِداً﴾, then He said: ﴿لِّتُؤْمِنُواْ﴾.
Its meaning is: that whoever believes may believe in you. And it has been said ليؤمنوا [with yāʾ], because the believer is other than the one addressed, so the meaning is: We have sent you so that they may believe in you. The meaning in the first is intended like this, even though it is like the one addressed, because you say to a group: "You have done [it]", while not all of them did it, i.e. some of you did; so this is evidence of that.
His saying: ﴿وَتُعَزِّرُوهُ﴾.
You support him with the sword; so it is reported from al-Kalbī.

farraa:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿يَدُ ٱللَّهِ فَوْقَ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾: in fulfilment and covenant.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿سَيَقُولُ لَكَ ٱلْمُخَلَّفُونَ مِنَ ٱلأَعْرَابِ﴾.
Those who stayed behind from al-Ḥudaybiya: "Our wealth and our families kept us busy." They were Bedouins: Aslam, Juhayna, Muzayna and Ghifār. They thought that the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him, would never return, so they stayed behind.
His saying: ﴿إِنْ أَرَادَ بِكُمْ ضَرّاً﴾.
Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb alone gave the ḍād ḍamma, and ʿĀṣim, the people of Medina and al-Ḥasan gave it fatḥa: "ضَراً".

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿أَن لَّن يَنقَلِبَ ٱلرَّسُولُ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِيهِمْ أَبَداً﴾; and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "إلى أهلهم", without yāʾ; and al-ahl is plural and singular.
His saying: ﴿وَكُنتُمْ قَوْماً بُوراً﴾.
[Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Ḥibbān narrated to me, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-būr in the dialect of Azd ʿUmān is the corrupt; "and you were a people būr": a corrupt people. And al-būr in the speech of the Arabs is: nothing. One says: "Their deeds became būr (naught) and their dwellings graves."

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿سَيَقُولُ ٱلْمُخَلَّفُونَ إِذَا ٱنطَلَقْتُمْ إِلَىٰ مَغَانِمَ لِتَأْخُذُوهَا﴾.
He means Khaybar, because Allah opened it to His Messenger straight after al-Ḥudaybiya. They said that to the Messenger of Allah: "Let us follow you." He said: "Yes, on condition that no share is given to you; if you go out on that basis, then go out." They said to the Muslims: "This is not yours; you have done this to us only out of envy." The Muslims said: "Thus Allah said to us before you said it."
His saying: ﴿يُرِيدُونَ أَن يُبَدِّلُواْ كلِمَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Yaḥyā alone read it (كَلِم), and the readers after him (كلام الله), with alif. Al-kalām is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and al-kalim is the plural of kalima. The meaning in His saying "يريدُونَ أن يبدلوا كلم الله" is: they hoped he would permit them, and so change the word of Allah. Then it was said: if you desire only raiding and jihād and not the spoils, you will be called tomorrow against the people of al-Yamāma, against a people of great might, the Banū Ḥanīfa, the followers of Musaylima. This is from the exegesis of al-Kalbī.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿تُقَاتِلُونَهُمْ أَوْ يُسْلِمُونَ﴾.
In one of the two readings: أو يُسْلِموا. And the meaning is: you will fight them forever until they submit; that is, unless they submit, you will fight them, or there will be [179/b] Islam from them.

farraa:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿لَّيْسَ عَلَى ٱلأَعْمَىٰ حَرَجٌ﴾: in abandoning the raid, to the end of the verse.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿تَحْتَ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ﴾: it was an acacia (samura).
His saying: ﴿فَعَلِمَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾.
The Prophet, Allah bless him, had been shown in his sleep that he would enter Mecca. When that was not made possible for him, and he made peace with the people of Mecca on the condition that they would vacate it for him for three days in the following year, a great matter came upon the Muslims. The Prophet, Allah bless him, said to them: "It was only a dream that I was shown, and it was not revelation from heaven." So He knew what was in their hearts, and sent down tranquillity (al-sakīna) upon them. Al-sakīna is reassurance and composure in what the Prophet, Allah bless him, told them: that it was for the following year. That is His saying: ﴿فَعَلِمَ ما لَمْ تَعْلَموا﴾: of the good of the dream's fulfilment.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿وَعَدَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ مَغَانِمَ كَثِيرَةً تَأْخُذُونَهَا﴾: of what will be after today; and He hastened this for you: Khaybar.
His saying: ﴿وَكَفَّ أَيْدِيَ ٱلنَّاسِ عَنْكُمْ﴾.
Asad and Ghaṭafān were with the people of Khaybar against the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him. The Prophet, Allah bless him, made for them, and they made peace with him, held back, and left him to deal with the people of Khaybar. That is His saying: ﴿وَكَفَّ أَيْدِيَ ٱلنَّاسِ عَنْكُمْ﴾.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأُخْرَىٰ لَمْ تَقْدِرُواْ عَلَيْهَا﴾.
Persia: Allah has encompassed it, encompassed it for you, to open it to you.

farraa:24-25.t:
His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي كَفَّ أَيْدِيَهُمْ عَنكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ عَنْهُم﴾.
This is for the people of al-Ḥudaybiya, not for the people of Khaybar.
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْهَدْيَ مَعْكُوفاً﴾: detained.
His saying: ﴿أَن يَبْلُغَ مَحِلَّهُ﴾: its place of slaughter, i.e. they barred the sacrificial animals.
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ رِجَالٌ مُّؤْمِنُونَ وَنِسَآءٌ مُّؤْمِنَاتٌ﴾.
There were Muslims in Mecca, so He said: were it not that you would kill them without knowing them, and a liability (maʿarra) would fall on you because of them, meaning the blood-money. Then Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿لَوْ تَزَيَّلُواْ﴾: had the unbelievers been separated and set apart from the believers, Allah would have sent down killing and punishment upon them.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿إِذْ جَعَلَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلْحَمِيَّةَ﴾.
They were roused by pride, [refusing] that the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him, should enter it upon them. So Allah sent down His tranquillity; he says: Allah removed from the believers [the danger] that the zealotry that entered those people should enter them, so that they would disobey Allah and His Messenger.
His saying: ﴿كَلِمَةَ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ﴾: "There is no god but Allah."
His saying: ﴿وَكَانُوۤاْ أَحَقَّ بِهَا وَأَهْلَهَا﴾.
I saw it in the codex of al-Ḥārith ibn Suwayd al-Taymī, one of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh: "وكانوا أهلها وأحق بها", and that is a fronting and postponing (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr). His codex was buried in the days of al-Ḥajjāj.

farraa:27-27.t:
His saying: ﴿لَتَدْخُلُنَّ ٱلْمَسْجِدَ [180/a] ٱلْحَرَامَ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ آمِنِينَ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: لا تخافون in place of آمنين; "مُحلِّقين رءوسكم ومُقَصِّرِينَ": had it been said محلقون ومقصرون, i.e. some of you shaving and some of you shortening, it would have been correct, [as] the poet said:
* وغودر البقل ملوى ومحصود *
(And the herbage was left, [some] withered and [some] harvested.)

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى ٱلدِّينِ كُلِّهِ﴾.
It is said: the world will not pass away until Islam prevails over the people of every religion, or they pay the jizya to them. That is His saying: ﴿لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّه﴾.

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿تَرَاهُمْ رُكَّعاً سُجَّداً﴾: in the prayer.
His saying: ﴿سِيمَاهُمْ فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ﴾: it is the pallor from staying awake at night.
His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ مَثَلُهُمْ فِي ٱلتَّوْرَاةِ﴾.
And in the Gospel also, like their likeness in the Qurʾān. And it is said: that is their likeness in the Torah, and their likeness in the Gospel is as a sown crop that puts forth its shoot (shaṭʾ); its shaṭʾ is the ears: the grain sprouts ten, eight and seven, and some of it strengthens the rest. That is His saying: (فآزره): it helped it and strengthened it; so [it] grew thick and stood upright; had it been one, it would not stand on a stalk. It is a parable Allah, Mighty and Majestic, struck for the Prophet, Allah bless him, when he went forth alone and then He strengthened him with his Companions, as He strengthened the grain with what sprouted from it.
Āzartu, uʾāziruhu, muʾāzaratan: I strengthened him and helped him; and that is al-muʾāzara.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليغفر» is genitive (majrūr) and attached to (mutaʿalliq) {فَتَحْنَا}; the preposition «من ذنبك» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تقدَّم»; «صراطا» is the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «إيمانا» is a tamyīz (specification); «مع» is an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «إيمانا». The clause «ولله جنود» is resumptive, as is the clause «وكان الله عليما»; «حكيما» is a second khabar (predicate) of «كان».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليدخل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied «يبتليكم»; «جنات» is the second object. The clause «وكان ذلك» ... is parenthetical, and the adverb «عند» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «فوزا».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «ويعذب» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {وَيُكَفِّرَ}; «الظانين» is a naʿt (adjective); «ظن» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) governed by «الظانين». The clause «عليهم دائرة» is resumptive, and the clause «وغضب الله» is conjoined to the clause «عليهم دائرة». The clause «وساءت مصيرا» is resumptive; the fāʿil (agent) of «ساءت» is latent (mustatir), referring to «جهنم»; «مصيرا» is a tamyīz (specification), and the one specified for blame is omitted, i.e. "Hell".

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «ولله جنود» is resumptive, as is the clause «وكان الله عزيزا».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «لتؤمنوا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {أَرْسَلْنَاكَ}; «بكرة» is an adverb of time attached to «تسبِّحوه».

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «إنما يبايعون» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ», and the clause «يد الله فوق أيديهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «يبايعونك». The clause «فمن نكث» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the resumptive clause «إن الذين ... », and «مَنْ» is conditional, mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause «ومن أوفى» is conjoined to the preceding conditional clause; the second «مَنْ» is conditional, mubtadaʾ, and the clause «أوفى» is its khabar. In the pronominal hāʾ of «عليه», after the yāʾ, both ḍamma and kasra are permissible; they are two dialects. One says both وفَّى and أَوْفى. «أجرًا» is the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The preposition «من الأعراب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «المخلفون»; the clause «فاستغفر» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «شغلتنا»; the clause «يقولون» is resumptive; «ما» is a relative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the preposition «في قلوبهم» is attached to the khabar (predicate) of «ليس». The maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying) is implied, i.e. "if Allah intends something for you", and the fāʾ in «فمن» occurs in the apodosis (jawāb) of the implied condition. The two prepositions «لكم» and «من الله» are attached to «يملك». The clause «إن أراد بكم ضرا» is resumptive, and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it; the preposition «بكم» is attached to a ḥāl from «ضرا». The clause «كان» is resumptive, and the preposition «بما» is attached to «خبيرا».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause «ظننتم» is resumptive. «أنْ» is lightened from the heavy form, and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from «أَنْ» and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «ظن». «أبدًا» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ينقلب». The clause «زُيِّن» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «ظننتم»; «ظنَّ» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); «بورا» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The clause «ومن لم يؤمن» is resumptive, and «مَنْ» is conditional, mubtadaʾ (subject). The preposition «للكافرين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أعتدنا», and the overt noun stands in place of the referring pronoun, i.e. "We have prepared for them".

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «ولله ملك» is resumptive; the clause «يغفر» is resumptive; and the clause «وكان» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The conditional clause is parenthetical; the clause «ذرونا» is the maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying); the clause «نتبعكم» is the apodosis (jawāb) of the implied condition; the clause «يريدون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «المخلفون», and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is the object of «يريدون». The kāf in «كذلكم» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "Allah said a saying like that". «قبل» is an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قال»; the clause «قال» is resumptive. The clause «فسيقولون» is resumptive, and the maqūl al-qawl is implied, i.e. "this is not from Allah"; the clause «تحسدوننا» is resumptive within the scope of the saying. The clause «كانوا» is resumptive, and «قليلا» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The preposition «من الأعراب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «المخلفين»; «أولي» is a naʿt (adjective) of «قوم»; the clause «تقاتلونهم» is a naʿt of «قوم»; and the conditional clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «سَتُدْعَوْن». «أجرا» is the second object. The kāf stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "a turning away like your turning away"; «ما» is maṣdariyya and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and «عذابا» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «ليس على الأعمى حرج» is resumptive within the scope of the saying; the conditional clause is resumptive; «جنات» is the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The clause «لقد رضي» is the answer to the oath; «إذ» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «رضي». The clause «فعلم» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «يبايعونك», and the clause «فأنزل» is conjoined to the clause «علم». «فتحا» is the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: «ومغانم» is a noun maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «فتحا»; the clause «يأخذونها» is a naʿt (adjective) of «مغانم»; and the clause «وكان الله عزيزًا حكيما» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «وعدكم» is resumptive; «مغانم» is the second object, and the clause «تأخذونها» is a naʿt (adjective) of «مغانم». The clause «فعجَّل» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «وعدكم». The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ولتكون» is genitive and attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied verb, i.e. "and so that it may be a sign, He did that", and the implied clause «فعل» is conjoined to the clause «كفّ». «صراطا» is the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: His words «وأخرى»: a noun maʿṭūf (conjoined) to {هَذِهِ}; the clause «لم تقدروا» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أخرى»; the clause «قد أحاط الله بها» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «عليها»; and the clause «وكان الله ... » is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The conditional clause is resumptive, and the clause «ثم لا يجدون» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: «سُنَّةَ» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "He ordained a practice", and the clause «ولن تجد» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «سَنَّ».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The clause «وهو الذي» is resumptive. The two prepositions «عنكم» and «عنهم» are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «كفَّ»; the preposition «ببطن» is attached to «كفَّ», as is «من بعد». «أن» is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the preposition «بما» is attached to «بصيرا».

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The clause «هم الذين» is resumptive. «الهدي» is a noun maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the kāf in «صدُّوكم»; «معكوفا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الهدي»; and the maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يبلغ» is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (ishtimāl) from «الهدي», i.e. "they barred the offering from reaching its place". The clause «ولولا رجال» is conjoined to the resumptive clause «هم الذين», and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. "He would have permitted you the conquest and given you power over the idolaters". The interpreted maṣdar «أن تَطَئوهم» is a badal from «رجال» and «نساء»; the preposition «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تصيبكم»; the preposition «بغير» is attached to a ḥāl from the kāf in «تصيبكم». The interpreted maṣdar «ليدخل» is genitive and attached to an omitted verb, i.e. "He did not permit the conquest so that He might admit". The conditional clause («لو» and what follows it) is resumptive, and the preposition «منهم» is attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «كفروا».

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: «إذ» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عذَّبنا». «جعل» here means "cast", transitive to one object, and the preposition «في قلوبهم» is attached to «جعل»; «حمية» is a badal (substitute). «كلمة» is the second object. The clause «وكانوا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «ألزمهم»; «وأهلها» is a noun conjoined to «أحقَّ». The clause «وكان الله ... » is resumptive, and the preposition «بكل» is attached to the khabar (predicate) «عليما».

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The clause «لقد صدق» is the response to the first, implied oath, and the clause of the oath and its response is resumptive. «الرؤيا» is the second object; the preposition «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الرؤيا». The clause «والله لتدخلُنَّ» explains the vision; the clause «لتدخلُن» is the answer to the oath; the verb is an imperfect, nominative (marfūʿ) by the presence of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of like letters, and the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil (agent). The clause «إن شاء الله» is parenthetical, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. «محلِّقين» is a second ḥāl, and «رءوسكم» is the object of «مُحَلِّقين». The clause «لا تخافون» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مقصِّرين». The clause «فعلم» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «صدق الله», and the preposition «من دون» is attached to the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The preposition «بالهدى» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «رسوله»; the genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليظهره» is attached to «أرسل». The clause «وكفى بالله» is resumptive; the Name of Majesty is the fāʿil (agent), the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and «شهيدا» is a tamyīz (specification).

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The clause «والذين معه أشداء» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the resumptive clause «محمد رسول الله». «معه»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause); the preposition «على الكفار» is attached to «أشداء»; «رحماء» is a second khabar (predicate) of «الذين»; the adverb «بينهم» is attached to «رحماء»; the clause «تراهم» is a third khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject); «سُجَّدا» is a second ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «تراهم»; the clause «يبتغون» is a fourth khabar; the preposition «من الله» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «فضلا»; the clause «سيماهم في وجوههم» is a fifth khabar; the preposition «من أثر» is attached to the notion of being (istiqrār) to which the khabar is attached. The clause «ذلك مثلهم» is resumptive, made up of mubtadaʾ and khabar; the preposition «في التوراة» is attached to a ḥāl from «مثلهم». The clause «ومثلهم كزرع» is conjoined to the clause «ذلك مثلهم»; the preposition «في الإنجيل» is attached to a ḥāl from «مثلهم»; the preposition «كزرع» is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the clause «أخرج» is a naʿt of «زرع»; and the clause «يعجب» is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «استوى». The genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليغيظ» is attached to an implied verb, i.e. "they were likened". The clause «وعد الله» is resumptive; the preposition «منهم» is attached to a ḥāl from the wāw of «عملوا»; «مغفرة» is the second object.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying, Exalted is He, {ويهديك صراطا مُسْتَقِيمًا}: that is, "to a path" (إلى صراط); then إلى was omitted, so الصِّرَاط became accusative because it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) in meaning.

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying {شَاهدا وَمُبشرا وَنَذِيرا}: the three are accusative as an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara, circumstantial), and they are circumstantial states of the كاف in أَرْسَلْنَاك; the governing word in them is أرسل, just as it is the governing word in the one the ḥāl describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl).

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying {إِن الَّذين يُبَايعُونَك}: the khabar (predicate) of إنّ is إنما يبايعون الله. It is also possible that the khabar is يَد الله فَوق أَيْديهم, which is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar in the position of the khabar of إنّ.

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying {تقاتلونهم أَو يسلمُونَ}: according to al-Kisāʾī, يسلمُونَ is conjoined to تقاتلون. Al-Zajjāj said it is resumptive, i.e. "or they will submit" (أو هم يسلمون). In the reading of Ubayy it is أَو يسلمُوا, in the accusative by an implied أنْ; its meaning according to the Basrans is "unless they submit" (إلا أن يسلموا), and al-Kisāʾī said its meaning is "until they submit" (حتى يسلموا).

mekki-muskil:21-21.t: His saying {وَأُخْرَى لم تقدروا}: أُخْرَى is in the position of the accusative by conjunction with مَغَانِم, and in the speech there is an omitted muḍāf; the implied form is "Allah promised you the possession of spoils and the possession of others" (وعدكم الله ملك مغانم وملك أخرى), because the second object of وعد can only be a maṣdar (verbal noun), since a promise does not fall on bodily things; it falls only on their possession and acquisition. You say وعدتك غلاما ("I promised you a slave-boy"): you did not promise him the person of the slave-boy, you only promised him possession of the person of a slave-boy.

mekki-muskil:23-23.t: His saying {سنة الله}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of {لولوا الأدبار} is "Allah has ordained their turning their backs as a practice (sunna), just as He ordained it for the disbelieving nations that passed away". In ordinary speech سنةٌ in the nominative is permissible, in the sense of "that is the practice", so you imply the mubtadaʾ (subject) and سنة is its khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:24-24.t: His saying {بِبَطن مَكَّة}: مَكَّة is a diptote because it is definite, a name for something feminine, namely the city.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t:
His saying {وَالْهَدْي معكوفا أَن يبلغ مَحَله}: الْهَدْي is accusative by conjunction with the كاف and the ميم in صدوكم, and أن is in the position of the accusative on the assumption of the omission of the preposition (accusative by removal of the preposition), i.e. "from reaching" (عن أن يبلغ).
His saying {وَلَوْلَا رجال مُؤمنُونَ وَنسَاء مؤمنات}: رجال is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), نسَاء is conjoined to them, and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "present" (بالحضرة), or "in the place" (بالموضع), or "in Mecca" (بمكة), and the like.
His saying {أَن تطؤوهم}: أن is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) of رجال or نسَاء, or in the position of the accusative as a badal of the هاء and the ميم in تعلموهم. The implied form on the first view is "were it not for your trampling believing men whom you did not know, so that guilt would befall you on account of them"; on the second view, "were it not for believing men whose trampling you did not know, so that it would befall you". In both cases it is a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl). The first view is clearer and stronger in meaning. Trampling (الوطء) here means killing.
And His saying {تعلموهم} is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of رجال and نسَاء, and the apodosis (jawāb) of لولا is omitted.

mekki-muskil:27-27.t: His saying {مُحَلِّقِينَ رؤوسكم وَمُقَصِّرِينَ}: two ḥāls (circumstantial) of the nominative latent pronoun in لتدخلن. The wāw is omitted from لتدخلن — it is the wāw of the plural pronoun — and it was omitted because it is quiescent and the first letter of the doubled consonant is quiescent. Likewise لا تخافون is also a ḥāl of them, i.e. "not fearing".

mekki-muskil:29-29.t:
His saying {مُحَمَّد رَسُول الله}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). {وَالَّذين مَعَه أشداء} is also a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and رحماء is a second khabar. So the statement of severity and mercy, and what follows it of their bowing and prostrating and the coining of parables about them, is about those who are with the Prophet; and the Prophet ﷺ is of a higher rank than them, because they attained this rank only through him and at his hands ﷺ.
It is also said: مُحَمَّد is a mubtadaʾ, رسول الله is a naʿt (adjective) of it, والذين معه is conjoined to مُحَمَّد, أشداء is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ about them all, and رحماء is a second khabar about them. So the Prophet, upon him be blessing and peace, is included in everything that is stated about them: severity, mercy, bowing, prostration and the parables mentioned. On the first view you pause on رسول الله ﷺ, and you do not pause on it on the second view.
His saying {ركعا سجدا}: two ḥāls (circumstantial) of the هاء and the ميم in {تراهم}, because it is from seeing with the eye; likewise {يَبْغُونَ} is also a ḥāl of them.
His saying {سِيمَاهُمْ}: a mubtadaʾ; {من أثر السُّجُود} is the khabar. It is also possible that the khabar is {فِي وُجُوههم}, and that is clearer and better.
His saying {ذَلِك مثلهم فِي التَّوْرَاة}: ذلك is a mubtadaʾ and مثلهم is the khabar.
His saying {وَمثلهمْ فِي الْإِنْجِيل}: conjoined to the first مثل; so you do not pause on التوراة if you make it [conjoined] to the first مثل. The meaning is then that they have been described in the Torah and the Gospel with these preceding attributes, and the كاف in His saying كزرع أخرج شطأه is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "they are like a sown field" (هم كزرع); so you begin with the كاف and pause on الإنجيل.
It is also possible that {وَمثلهمْ فِي الْإِنْجِيل} is a mubtadaʾ and كزرع the khabar; then you pause on التوراة and begin with ومثلهم في الإنجيل كزرع, and you do not pause on الإنجيل nor begin with the كاف on this view, because it is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. The meaning is then that they have been described in the two Books with two descriptions: they were described in the Torah as being severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves, you see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and good pleasure, and that their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration; and they were described in the Gospel as being like a sown field that puts forth its shoot, to the end of the description. The first view is the view of Mujāhid, and the second is the view of al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Qatāda.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿إنا فتحنا لك﴾: إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); ﴿نا﴾: its noun; the clause فتحنا is its khabar (predicate); لك: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿فتحنا﴾.
﴿فتحًا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
﴿مبينًا﴾: an adjective.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿إن الذين يبايعونك إنما يبايعون الله﴾: إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); الذين: its noun; the clause ﴿يبايعونك﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. إنما: [إنّ] made inoperative (makfūfa) by the preventing [mā] (kāffa); the clause إنما يبايعون الله is the khabar (predicate) of إن; what is meant by this pledge is the Pledge of Riḍwān at al-Ḥudaybiya.
﴿يد الله فوق أيديهم﴾: يد الله: mubtadaʾ (subject); فوق أيديهم: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar of يد الله; the clause is a second khabar of ﴿إن﴾, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) pronoun in يبايعونك, or also resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿فمن نكث فإنما ينكث﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; من: a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ; نكث: a past verb in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ; إنما: [إنّ] made inoperative by the preventing [mā]; ينكث: an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), implied as "he"; the clause ﴿فمن نكث...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿على نفسه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ينكث﴾; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
﴿ومن أوفى بما عاهد عليه الله﴾: the wāw is a conjunction particle; من: a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ; أوفى: the protasis; بما: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أوفى; the clause عاهد is the ṣila, with no grammatical position. عليه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to عاهد; the Name of Majesty is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿فسيؤتيه أجرًا عظيما﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis; يؤتيه: a verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; أجرًا: a second mafʿūl bihi; عظيمًا: a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿سيقول لك المخلفون من الأعراب شغلتنا أموالنا وأهلونا﴾: the sīn is a particle of the future; يقول: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); لك is attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يقول﴾; المخلفون: fāʿil (agent); من الأعراب: a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause شغلتنا أموالنا is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); أهلونا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أموالنا, the sign of its nominative being the wāw, because it is treated as a sound masculine plural (mulḥaq bi-jamʿ al-mudhakkar al-sālim).
﴿فاستغفر لنا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; استغفر: an imperative verb; لنا: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to استغفر; the object of استغفر is omitted, i.e. the Name of Majesty الله.
﴿يقولون بألسنتهم ما ليس في قلوبهم﴾: the clause is the object of the saying of Allah the Exalted; يقولون: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; بألسنتهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يقولون; ما: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ليس: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun latent (mustatir), implied as "it"; في قلوبهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate). The clause ﴿ليس في قلوبهم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿قل فمن يملك لكم من الله شيئا إن أراد بكم ضرا أو أراد بكم نفعا﴾: قل: an imperative verb; the fāʾ is a conjunction; من: an interrogative noun whose meaning is negation, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); يملك: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent, implied as "he"; the clause is the khabar of من, and the [whole] clause is the object of قل; لكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يملك; من الله: a ḥāl; شيئًا: the object of يملك; إن: a conditional particle; أراد: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then who has power…"; بكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أراد; خيرًا: the object of أراد [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in this part of the ayah is ﴿ضرا﴾]; the clause أو أراد بكم نفعًا is conjoined to the preceding clause.
﴿بل كان الله بما تعملون خبيرا﴾: بل: a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī), moving from one topic to another; كان: a defective past verb; the Name of Majesty is its noun; بما: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خبيرًا﴾; the clause ﴿تعملون﴾ is the ṣila, with no grammatical position; خبيرًا: the khabar of كان.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿بل﴾: also a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī).
﴿ظننتم﴾: a verb and its fāʿil (agent).
﴿أن﴾: أن is lightened from the heavy form (mukhaffafa), its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the clause ﴿لن يخرج...﴾ is its khabar (predicate) [Translator's note: so in the source, apparently carried over from Q 47:29; the clause here is ﴿لن ينقلب...﴾]; أن with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of ظننتم.
﴿لن﴾: a particle of negation, the accusative and the future.
﴿ينقلب﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by لن.
﴿الرسول﴾: fāʿil.
﴿والمؤمنون﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الرسول.
﴿إلى أهليهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينقلب﴾.
﴿أبدًا﴾: an adverb, also attached to ﴿ينقلب﴾.
﴿وزين﴾: a passive past verb (built for an unnamed agent).
﴿ذلك﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
﴿في قلوبكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿زين﴾.
﴿وظننتم﴾: conjoined to وزين.
﴿ظن﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
﴿السوء﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿وكنتم﴾: كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the tāʾ is its noun.
﴿قومًا﴾: its khabar.
﴿بورًا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿قومًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿ومن لم يؤمن بالله ورسوله﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, confirming their ruin; من: a jussive conditional noun, or a relative noun, in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject); لم: a particle of negation, of conversion [to past meaning] and of the jussive; يؤمن: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم; بالله: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يؤمن﴾; رسوله is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الله; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. "then he is a disbeliever".
﴿فإنا أعتدنا للكافرين سعيرا﴾: the fāʾ conjoins to the apodosis; إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); ﴿نا﴾: its noun; the clause أعتدنا is the khabar (predicate) of إن; للكافرين: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أعتدنا﴾; سعيرًا: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the conditional clause with its apodosis is the khabar of من if it is conditional, and the clause فإنا أعتدنا is the khabar if it is a relative noun, the fāʾ entering because of the sense of condition contained in the relative noun.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿ولله ملك السماوات والأرض يغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لله: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); ملك السماوات والأرض: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause يغفر is a ḥāl (circumstantial); لمن: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يغفر﴾; the clause يشاء is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. ويعذب من يشاء is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause of the ṣila.
﴿وكان الله غفورا رحيما﴾: كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the Name of Majesty is its noun; غفورا: its first khabar; رحيمًا: its second khabar.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿سيقول المخلفون إذا انطلقتم إلى مغانم لتأخذوها ذرونا نتبعكم﴾: the sīn is a particle of the future; يقول المخلفون: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); إذا: a future adverb containing the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يقول; the clause انطلقتم is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the adverb's annexation to it; إلى مغانم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to انطلقتم; the clause ذرونا is the object of their saying, i.e. "let us"; نتبعكم: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab).
﴿يريدون أن يبدلوا كلام الله﴾: the clause يريدون is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil, namely المخلفون, and you may make it resumptive, with no grammatical position; it has also been said: a ḥāl from the object pronoun in ﴿ذرونا﴾, but this is strained and far-fetched; أن and what follows it are the object of يريدون; كلام الله: the object of يبدلوا.
﴿قل لن تتبعونا كذلكم قال الله﴾: قل: an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), implied as "you"; لن: a particle of negation, the accusative and the future; تتبعونا: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by ﴿لن﴾, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and نا is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿كذلكم﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning مثل ("like"), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a saying like this saying issuing from me"; ﴿ذلكم﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the lām is for distance, the kāf is a particle of address, and the mīm is for the plural; ﴿قال﴾: a past verb; the Name of Majesty is the fāʿil.
﴿من قبل﴾: من: a preposition; ﴿قبل﴾: an adverb of time, indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿قال﴾.
﴿فسيقولون بل تحسدوننا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; the sīn is a particle of the future; يقولون: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); بل: a particle of digression (iḍrāb), or of conjunction; تحسدوننا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿سيقولون﴾; it is an imperfect verb, nominative, a fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi.
﴿بل كانوا لا يفقهون﴾: بل: a second digression, away from describing them as attributing envy to the believers, to what is worse than that, namely ignorance; كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the wāw of the group is its noun; the clause لا يفقهون is its khabar (predicate).
﴿إلا قليلا﴾: إلا: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); قليلًا: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "except a little understanding".

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿قل﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "you".
﴿للمخلفين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قل﴾.
﴿من الأعراب﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿ستدعون﴾: the clause ستدعون is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿إلى قوم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تدعون﴾.
﴿أولي بأس شديد﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿قوم﴾.
﴿تقاتلونهم أو يسلمون﴾: the clause تقاتلونهم is a second naʿt, or a ḥāl, or resumptive, with no grammatical position; أو: a conjunction particle; يسلمون is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to تقاتلونهم; and you may take the imperfect verb as nominative (marfūʿ) by way of resumption, the implied form being: أو هم يسلمون ("or they submit").
﴿فإن تطيعوا يؤتكم الله أجرا حسنا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; إن: conditional; تطيعوا: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; يؤتكم: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الله: fāʿil; أجرًا: the second mafʿūl bihi; حسنًا: a naʿt of ﴿أجرًا﴾.
﴿وإن تتولوا كما توليتم من قبل يعذبكم عذابا أليما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إن: conditional; تتولوا: the protasis; ﴿كما﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning مثل ("like"), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya (infinitival); ﴿توليتم﴾: a verb and its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar from the maṣdariyya ﴿ما﴾ and the verb is muḍāf ilayhi; من قبل: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to توليتم; قبل is indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording, not in meaning; يعذبكم: the apodosis; the kāf is its object; عذابا stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar); أليمًا: a naʿt of ﴿عذابًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿ليس على الأعمى حرج ولا على الأعرج حرج ولا على المريض حرج﴾: ليس: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; على الأعرج [Translator's note: so in the source; the first phrase after ليس is ﴿على الأعمى﴾]: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of ليس; حرج: its postponed noun; and what follows is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it.
﴿ومن يطع الله ورسوله يدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار﴾: the wāw is a conjunction particle; من: conditional, in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject); يطع الله ورسوله: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); يدخله: its apodosis (jawāb); جنات: a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa); the clause تجري من تحتها الأنهار is an adjective of ﴿جنات﴾.
﴿ومن يتول يعذبه عذابا أليما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; من: conditional, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; يتول: the protasis; يعذبه: its apodosis; عذابا stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar); أليما: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عذابا﴾, accusative.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿لقد رضي الله عن المؤمنين إذ يبايعونك تحت الشجرة﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to an implied oath; قد: a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); رضي الله: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); عن المؤمنين: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿رضي﴾; إذ: an adverb of past time, attached to ﴿رضي﴾; the clause يبايعونك is in the position of genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi; تحت الشجرة: an adverb attached to ﴿يبايعونك﴾.
﴿فعلم ما في قلوبهم فأنزل السكينة عليهم وأثابهم فتحا قريبا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; علم: a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), implied as "he", referring to Allah the Exalted; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to يبايعونك, given what was said earlier, that it has the sense of the past; ما: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); في قلوبهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. فأنزل is conjoined to فعلم; السكينة: mafʿūl bihi; أثابهم is also conjoined; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi; فتحًا: the second mafʿūl bihi; قريبًا: a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿ومغانم كثيرة يأخذونها﴾: the wāw is a conjunction particle; مغانم is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿فتحًا قريبًا﴾; the clause يأخذونها is an adjective of ﴿مغانم﴾.
﴿وكان الله عزيزا حكيما﴾: كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the Name of Majesty is its noun; عزيزًا: the first khabar (predicate) of كان; حكيمًا: the second khabar of كان.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿ليغفر لك الله ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر﴾: the lām is causal (taʿlīl); يغفر: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿فتحنا﴾; لك: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يغفر﴾; الله: fāʿil (agent); ما: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿تقدم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. من ذنبك: a ḥāl (circumstantial); وما تأخر is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ما تقدم.
﴿ويتم نعمته عليك ويهديك صراطا مستقيما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; يتم is conjoined to ليغفر; نعمته: mafʿūl bihi; عليك: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to نعمته or to يتم; يهديك is also conjoined; the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi; صراطًا: the second mafʿūl bihi, or accusative by removal of the preposition; مستقيمًا: a naʿt (adjective), accusative by the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿وعدكم الله مغانم كثيرة تأخذونها﴾: وعدكم الله: a past verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and a postponed fāʿil (agent); مغانم: a second mafʿūl bihi; كثيرة: an adjective; the clause تأخذونها is a second adjective.
﴿فعجل لكم هذه وكف أيدي الناس عنكم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; عجل: a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), referring to Allah; لكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) عجل; هذه: mafʿūl bihi; وكف أيدي الناس عنكم is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes.
﴿ولتكون آية للمؤمنين ويهديكم صراطا مستقيما﴾: the wāw conjoins to something implied, i.e. "so that you may thank Him"; the noun of ﴿تكون﴾ is a latent pronoun, implied as "it" (hiya); آية: its khabar (predicate); للمؤمنين: a naʿt (adjective) of آية; يهديكم is conjoined to ولتكون; the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi; صراطًا: the second mafʿūl bihi; مستقيمًا: an accusative naʿt of ﴿صراطا﴾.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿وأخرى لم تقدروا عليها قد أحاط الله بها﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أخرى is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to هذه; it has also been said: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause لم تقدروا عليها being its adjective and the clause قد أحاط الله بها its khabar (predicate); and it has been said: ﴿أخرى﴾ is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied verb indicated by ﴿قد أحاط الله بها﴾, its implied form being: "وقضى الله أخرى قد أحاط بها" ("and Allah decreed another which He has encompassed"). And it has been said: it is genitive (majrūr) by an implied رُبّ, the wāw being the wāw of rubba, with ﴿لم تقدروا﴾ an adjective and ﴿قد أحاط﴾ the khabar.
﴿وكان الله على كل شيء قديرا﴾: كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the Name of Majesty is its noun; قديرًا: its khabar; ﴿على كل شيء﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قديرًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿ولو قاتلكم الذين كفروا﴾: the wāw is resumptive; لو: conditional; قاتلكم: a verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الذين: fāʿil (agent); the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿لولوا﴾: the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; ولوا: a verb and its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb) of لو.
﴿الأدبار﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿ولو قاتلكم الذين...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿ثم لا يجدون وليا ولا نصيرا﴾: ثم: a conjunction particle; لا: negative; يجدون: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and its fāʿil; وليًّا: mafʿūl bihi; ولا نصيرًا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿سنة الله التي قد خلت من قبل﴾: a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) by an implied verb from its own root, i.e. سنَّ الله ذلك سنة ("Allah established that as a practice"). The Name of Majesty: muḍāf ilayhi. التي: a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿سنة﴾. The clause ﴿قد خلت﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿التي﴾, with no grammatical position. من قبل: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خلت﴾; and the wāw is a conjunction.
﴿ولن تجد لسنة الله تبديلا﴾: لن: a particle of negation, the accusative and the future; تجد: an imperfect verb, accusative by ﴿لن﴾; لسنة الله: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تجد﴾; تبديلًا: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿وهو الذي كف أيديهم عنكم وأيديكم عنهم ببطن مكة من بعد أن أظفركم عليهم﴾: the wāw is resumptive; هو: mubtadaʾ (subject); الذي: its khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿كَفَّ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. أيديهم: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); عنكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) كف; the clause ﴿وهو الذي...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; وأيديكم عنهم is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أيديهم عنكم; ببطن مكة: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being in the valley of Mecca"; من بعد: a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to كف; أن with what falls within its scope is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation to the adverb; عليهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أظفركم﴾.
﴿وكان الله بما تعملون بصيرا﴾: كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the Name of Majesty is its noun; بصيرًا: its khabar; بما تعملون: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿بصيرًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿هم الذين كفروا وصدوكم عن المسجد الحرام والهدي معكوفا﴾: هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); الذين: its khabar (predicate); the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position; صدوكم is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the ṣila; عن المسجد: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) صدوكم; الحرام: a naʿt (adjective). الهدي is conjoined to the accusative pronoun in صدوكم, or it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), the wāw being for accompaniment (maʿiyya); معكوفًا: a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿أن يبلغ محله﴾: أن with what falls within its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar, accusative (manṣūb) by removal of the preposition, i.e. عن أن يبلغ or من أن يبلغ ("from reaching"), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to صدوكم or to ﴿معكوفًا﴾. Or the interpreted maṣdar is accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), because it is the reason for the barring, the implied form being: "صدوا الهدي كراهة أن يبلغ محله" ("they barred the offering, disliking that it should reach its place"); or it is the reason for ﴿معكوفًا﴾. Some parsed it as a badal (substitute) of inclusion (ishtimāl) from الهدي, i.e. "barring the offering's reaching its place".
﴿ولولا رجال مؤمنون ونساء مؤمنات لم تعلموهم أن تطئوهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لولا: a particle of non-occurrence due to existence (imtināʿ li-wujūd); رجال: a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "موجودون بمكة" ("present in Mecca"); مؤمنون: a naʿt of رجال; نساء مؤمنات is conjoined to ﴿رجال مؤمنون﴾; the clause لم تعلموهم is an adjective of the men and the women together; أن with what falls within its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar, a badal of inclusion from رجال and نساء, or from the attached pronoun in ﴿تعلموهم﴾.
﴿فتصيبكم منهم معرة بغير علم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; تصيبكم: an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to تطئوهم; the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the mīm the sign of the plural; منهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to تصيبكم; معرة: the fāʿil (agent) of تصيبكم; بغير علم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from the kāf, or to an omitted adjective of معرة.
﴿ليدخل الله في رحمته من يشاء﴾: the lām is causal (taʿlīl); يدخل: an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to something implied, i.e. "the absence of [your being given] power over the people of Mecca came about [so that…]"; في رحمته: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يدخل; من يشاء: mafʿūl bihi; the clause يشاء is the ṣila, with no grammatical position.
﴿لو تزيلوا لعذبنا الذين كفروا منهم عذابا أليما﴾: لو: conditional; تزيلوا: a past verb and its fāʿil; the lām is the linking lām; the clause عذبنا has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb) of لو; عذبنا: a verb and its fāʿil; الذين كفروا: mafʿūl bihi; منهم: a ḥāl; عذابا stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar); أليمًا: an adjective.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿إذ جعل الذين كفروا في قلوبهم الحمية حمية الجاهلية﴾: ﴿إذ﴾: an adverb of past time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿عذبنا﴾ or to ﴿صدوكم﴾; or ﴿إذ﴾ is a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, implied as اذكر ("remember"); the clause ﴿جعل﴾ is in the position of genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi; الذين: fāʿil (agent); the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position; في قلوبهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to جعل if it means "cast", or to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of جعل if it means "made [to become]"; الحمية: the first mafʿūl bihi; حمية الجاهلية: a badal (substitute).
﴿فأنزل الله سكينته على رسوله وعلى المؤمنين وألزمهم كلمة التقوى﴾: the fāʾ conjoins to something implied that must be supplied, understood from the context; فأنزل الله: a verb and its fāʿil; سكينته: mafʿūl bihi; على رسوله: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أنزل﴾; وعلى المؤمنين is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes; ألزمهم is also conjoined; the hāʾ is the first object; كلمة التقوى: the second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿وكانوا أحق بها وأهلها﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿كانوا﴾: كان and its noun. أحق: the khabar (predicate) of كان. بها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أحق﴾. أهلها: conjoined to ﴿أحق﴾, accusative.
﴿وكان الله بكل شيء عليما﴾: كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the Name of Majesty is its noun; بكل شيء: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿عليمًا﴾; عليمًا: the khabar of كان.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿لقد صدق الله رسوله الرؤيا بالحق﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to an implied oath; قد: a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); صدق الله: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); رسوله: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الرؤيا: accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "in his vision"; and it has been said: صدق takes two objects; بالحق: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) صدق, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الرؤيا.
﴿لتدخلن المسجد الحرام﴾: the lām: the answer to an omitted oath; تدخلن: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of a succession of identical letters, since it is one of the five verbs; the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil; the nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis; المسجد: mafʿūl bihi by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa); الحرام: an adjective.
﴿إن شاء الله﴾: إن: conditional; ﴿شاء﴾: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. The Name of Majesty: fāʿil, nominative. The conditional clause ﴿إن شاء الله﴾ is parenthetical, with no grammatical position.
﴿آمنين محلقين رءوسكم ومقصرين لا تخافون﴾: آمنين: a ḥāl from the wāw dropped from ﴿لتدخلن﴾ because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, i.e. a ḥāl concurrent with the entering. محلقين: a second, overlapping (mutadākhila) ḥāl; رؤوسكم: mafʿūl bihi; لا: negative; تخافون: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or a ḥāl from the fāʿil of لتدخلن, or from the pronoun in آمنين, or in محلقين.
﴿فعلم ما لم تعلموا فجعل من دون ذلك فتحا قريبا﴾: the fāʾ conjoins to the clause صدق الله; علم: a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), implied as "he"; ما: mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿لم تعلموا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position. فجعل: the fāʾ is a conjunction; من دون ذلك: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to جعل; فتحًا: mafʿūl bihi; قريبًا: a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿هو﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿الذي﴾: its khabar (predicate).
﴿أرسل رسوله﴾: the clause أرسل رسوله is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿بالهدى﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "clothed with guidance".
﴿ودين الحق﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الهدى.
﴿ليظهره﴾: the lām is causal (taʿlīl); يظهره: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أرسل.
﴿على الدين كله﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿أرسل﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; one would expect ﴿يظهره﴾]; كله: a tawkīd (emphasis) of الدين; the ﴿أل﴾ in الدين is generic (for the genus), meaning the various religions.
﴿وكفى بالله شهيدا﴾: كفى: a past verb; the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) particle; the Name of Majesty is genitive in wording and the fāʿil (agent) of كفى in position; شهيدًا: a tamyīz (specification).

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿محمد رسول الله﴾: محمد: mubtadaʾ (subject); رسول الله: its khabar (predicate).
﴿والذين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; الذين: a relative noun in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ.
﴿معه﴾: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position.
﴿أشداء﴾: khabar.
﴿على الكفار﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أشداء﴾.
﴿رحماء﴾: a second khabar.
﴿بينهم﴾: an adverb attached to ﴿رحماء﴾.
